עיצוב UX/UI של מוצר עבור

עיצוב יצירתי מושך אנשים, חוויית משתמש חכמה גורמת להם להישאר

לסטארט-אפים וחברות בינלאומיות, מתמחים בגיימינג, רפואה, סייבר, IoT, אגריטק, אפליקציות, ופלטפורמות-SaaS


למה סטארט-אפים וחברות היי-טק גלובליות משתפות איתנו פעולה...

יזמים ומנהלי מוצר זקוקים לנסיון והתמחות וורטיקלית. לטריאולה מחלקות מתמחות בסייבר סקיוריטי, מדיקל, פינטק, אגרו, מערכות מורכבות

אנשים שאלו אותנו

ריכזנו עבורכם כמה שאלות ותשובות נפוצות כדי להקל עליכם ולחסוך לכם זמן


האם תוכל לעזור גם בעיצוב UX וגם בעיצוב UI?


בהחלט. אנו מספקים שירותי עיצוב UX (חוויית משתמש) ועיצוב UI (ממשק משתמש), ומלווים אתכם בכל שלבי התהליך – מהאפיון ועד לעיצוב הסופי.


איך אתם מוודאים שהעיצובים שלכם מתאימים למותג שלי?


כחברה שעובדת עם החברות ומותגים המובילוים בעולם, יש לנו הרבה נסיון בעיצוב חווית משתמש שהיא בהתאמה מלאה ומעצימה את מיתוג החברות


האם ניתן לעצב מחדש מוצר קיים?


כן, אנו הרבה מאוד פרויקטים שלנו, אנחנו עושים מתיחת פנים ו/או ממשיכים בעיצוב ופיתוח המוצר, נבצע ניתוח מעמיק של המוצר הנוכחי, נאתר נקודות לשיפור, ונבנה חוויית משתמש ועיצוב עדכניים ומותאמים לצרכים שלכם.


האם אתם עורכים מחקרי משתמשים כחלק מהשירותים שלכם?


כן וודאי! אנו מבצעים מחקרי משתמשים כחלק בלתי נפרד מתהליך העבודה. המחקר מסייע לנו להבין את הצרכים, ההרגלים והאתגרים של קהל היעד, ולבנות חוויית משתמש מדויקת ותואמת את צרכי המשתמש.


כמה זמן לוקח בדרך כלל תהליך עיצוב מוצר?


משך תהליך עיצוב מוצר משתנה בהתאם להיקף ולמורכבות הפרויקט. לרוב, תהליך מלא כולל אפיון, עיצוב UX/UI ובדיקות משתמשים, ונמשך בין מספר שבועות לכמה חודשים. אנו מתאימים את לוחות הזמנים לצרכים ולדרישות של כל לקוח.


עם אילו תעשיות עבדת?


יחודיותה של טריאולה היא שיש לנו ממש מחלקות מתמחות: סייבר, רפואה ובריאות, פינטק ופיננסים, גיימינג, אגריטק ו-IoT, יש לנו נסיון בעבודה עם סטארטאפים וחברות גלובליות. יש לנו נסיון באפליקציות מובייל, פלטפורמות SaaS, B2B ו-B2C.


מה עלות העבודה עם טריאולה?


העלות משתנה בהתאם להיקף הפרויקט, מורכבות הממשק, מספר המסכים והדרישות הייחודיות. בדרך כלל, סטודיו מקצועי יספק הצעת מחיר מותאמת לאחר הערכה ראשונית. ב-Triolla, עלות ממוצעת לעיצוב UX נעה בין 15,000 ל-40,000 דולר.

הכירו את טריאולה


מהקונספט ועד להשקת המוצר

צוות החלומות שלך: מעצבי UX/UI, מומחי AI, ומפתחי Front & Back-End ברמה הגבוהה ביותר....


אנחנו המנוע שמאחורי כמה מהמוצרים הדיגיטליים החדשניים והמובילים בישראל ובעולם. עם שילוב ייחודי של מומחיות עיצוב, טכנולוגיה ופיתוח, אנו מלווים אותך מהרעיון הראשוני ועד למוצר עובד בשוק – מהיר, מאובטח ובעל ביצועים יוצאי דופן. עובדים עם יוניקורנים, סטארטאפים בצמיחה מואצת ומובילי תעשייה – כדי להפוך חלומות גדולים למוצרים שמנצחים בשוק.


Triolla - טריאולה : הבחירה המובילה בישראל למוצרי UX/UI, עם פיתוח Full-Stack מקצה לקצה להצלחת השקת המוצר שלך.

למעלה מ-65 מומחי עיצוב  מוצר וצוותי פיתוח Full-Stack, עם ניסיון של למעלה מעשור, אנחנו הצוות מאחורי מאות אפליקציות ופלטפורמות עבור המותגים המובילים בעולם.


חלק מ                    Triolla נרכשה על ידי SQLink, אחת מחמשת האינטגרטורים הגדולים בישראל, עם למעלה מ-2,800 עובדים – מה שמעניק לנו בסיס איתן וביטחון לצמוח בגדול, באומץ ובחוכמה.


Triolla Academy, המכללה הרביעית בגודלה בארץ, מכשירה את הדור הבא של מעצבי מוצר, מנהלי מוצר ומנהלי פרויקטים

אנו מעצבים ומפתחים מערכות, פלטפורמות ואפליקציות לחברות המצליחות בעולם

למה סטארט-אפים וחברות היי-טק גלובליות משתפות איתנו פעולה...

חברות בוחרות ב-Triolla בזכות המומחיות העמוקה שלנו, הניסיון הרב, והאנשים המוכשרים ביותר בתעשייה. אנו מציעים מחלקות ייעודיות בתחומי הסייבר, הפינטק, הרפואה והגיימינג – ומבטיחים פתרונות ברמה הגבוהה ביותר לפלטפורמות מורכבות.

עיצובמפורט


למידה. חקירה. צמיחה אישית.

בטריאולה, צמיחה היא גישה. זו הסיבה שאנו מתדלקים את תרבות הארגונית שלנו עם הרצאות לאורך כל השנה, מפגשי מומחים ולמידה בלתי פוסקת.


- עיצוב מוצר מונע בינה מלאכותית: שילוב למידת מכונה לחוויות דיגיטליות חדשניות

- מחקר UX מתקדם: שליטה בראיונות משתמשים ובבדיקות למוצרים אהובים.

- פיתוח מוצרים מאובטח: יסודות אבטחת סייבר לבניית פלטפורמות דיגיטליות בטוחות.

- מיתוג למוצרים דיגיטליים: צור סיפורים וזהויות חזותיות מרתקות.

- יצירת אב טיפוס מהירה: איטרציה מהירה ואימות של רעיונות למוצר.

- חוויית משתמש פינטק: עיצוב מוצרים פיננסיים ידידותיים למשתמש עם אבטחה.

- ויזואליזציה של נתונים: הפיכת נתונים מורכבים לתצוגות ויזואליות ברורות ומושכות.

- עיצוב שכנוע: השפעה אתית על התנהגות המשתמש באמצעות חוויית משתמש מושכלת.


הלקוחות שלנו

מחברות קטנות ועד גלובליות, שיתפנו פעולה עם כמה חברות מדהימות


בוא נדבר
בוא נדבר


אנשים שאלו אותנו

ריכזנו עבורכם כמה שאלות ותשובות נפוצות כדי להקל עליכם ולחסוך לכם זמן


האם תוכל לעזור גם בעיצוב UX וגם בעיצוב UI?


בהחלט. אנו מספקים שירותי עיצוב UX (חוויית משתמש) ועיצוב UI (ממשק משתמש), ומלווים אתכם בכל שלבי התהליך – מהאפיון ועד לעיצוב הסופי.


איך אתם מוודאים שהעיצובים שלכם מתאימים למותג שלי?


כחברה שעובדת עם החברות ומותגים המובילוים בעולם, יש לנו הרבה נסיון בעיצוב חווית משתמש שהיא בהתאמה מלאה ומעצימה את מיתוג החברות


האם ניתן לעצב מחדש מוצר קיים?


כן, אנו הרבה מאוד פרויקטים שלנו, אנחנו עושים מתיחת פנים ו/או ממשיכים בעיצוב ופיתוח המוצר, נבצע ניתוח מעמיק של המוצר הנוכחי, נאתר נקודות לשיפור, ונבנה חוויית משתמש ועיצוב עדכניים ומותאמים לצרכים שלכם.


האם אתם עורכים מחקרי משתמשים כחלק מהשירותים שלכם?


כן וודאי! אנו מבצעים מחקרי משתמשים כחלק בלתי נפרד מתהליך העבודה. המחקר מסייע לנו להבין את הצרכים, ההרגלים והאתגרים של קהל היעד, ולבנות חוויית משתמש מדויקת ותואמת את צרכי המשתמש.


כמה זמן לוקח בדרך כלל תהליך עיצוב מוצר?


משך תהליך עיצוב מוצר משתנה בהתאם להיקף ולמורכבות הפרויקט. לרוב, תהליך מלא כולל אפיון, עיצוב UX/UI ובדיקות משתמשים, ונמשך בין מספר שבועות לכמה חודשים. אנו מתאימים את לוחות הזמנים לצרכים ולדרישות של כל לקוח.


עם אילו תעשיות עבדת?


יחודיותה של טריאולה היא שיש לנו ממש מחלקות מתמחות: סייבר, רפואה ובריאות, פינטק ופיננסים, גיימינג, אגריטק ו-IoT, יש לנו נסיון בעבודה עם סטארטאפים וחברות גלובליות. יש לנו נסיון באפליקציות מובייל, פלטפורמות SaaS, B2B ו-B2C.


מה עלות העבודה עם טריאולה?


העלות משתנה בהתאם להיקף הפרויקט, מורכבות הממשק, מספר המסכים והדרישות הייחודיות. בדרך כלל, סטודיו מקצועי יספק הצעת מחיר מותאמת לאחר הערכה ראשונית. ב-Triolla, עלות ממוצעת לעיצוב UX נעה בין 15,000 ל-40,000 דולר.

Six Things You Need to Check Before Hiring a UX/UI Agency


Choosing a UX/UI design agency presents its own challenges because it's a core component of your product and how you want your customers to experience it. When it comes to the product, the customer is still king.


Choosing a UX/UI design agency presents its own challenges because it’s a core component of your product success. The customer is king when it comes to product adoption and engagement, and this is the arena where you should win your battles. The pandemic has pushed forward drastic changes in customer behavior, and the “stickiness” of these changes will depend largely on customer satisfaction. As such, one of your business goals should be creating a product that would provide a seamless and intuitive experience to your users.


This is where UX and UI design come in.


Each concept is complex in itself; combined, they can be a source of frustration even for those who understand the core concepts of user experience and user interface. Building an engaging product or mobile application that’s also well optimized can be very challenging, but hiring a UX/UI design agency ensures that your application is, aside from being aesthetically pleasing, quick and easy to browse, reliable, and rich with features that improve the overall user experience.


Finding the Right UX/UI Design Agency for Your Business


To ensure that your design philosophy conforms to your business goals, you should find an agency that understands your business inside out. This means that you yourself should have a deep understanding of your business and what it stands for, including how you want it presented to prospects and customers. The aesthetics, functionality, and ease of use of your product is your best tool for making a good first impression and attracting the right audience. Ensure that it represents your business, its value proposition, and how this is offered to your customers through its content and overall design and structure.


It’s best to create a list of must-haves and things to consider before working with a UX/UI design agency to help you identify salient points and things you need to discuss with potential providers. Below is a list of things to consider before you jump into a partnership with an agency.


[contact-form-7 id=”958e338″ title=”Post Contact Form”]


#1 Agency Proficiency 
If you’re working on a product, it’s only logical to find a UX/UI design agency that specializes in products. A product-oriented company with vast experience will deliver value that goes beyond your expectations. It also aligns both your expectations when it comes to project constraints. Most project parameters will obviously be dependent on the product, so a product focus will definitely prove beneficial for both parties.


#2 Availability
Availability is an important factor because your timelines will be largely dependent on how available and flexible your UX/UI design agency is. Not everybody is available to start a new project immediately and give it the attention you require. However, the details should be clear at the onset so the agency knows what needs to be done and when it should be completed. The agency should be able to provide an estimate of when a project will be completed.


#3 Vertical Expertise
If you’re looking for a personalized touch, you should look for a UX/UI design agency that has significant experience in your specific vertical. This ensures that it has a deeper understanding of your business, what it does, and the markets it serves. An agency that demonstrates real experience in your domain can provide a personalized touch peppered with relevant expertise and experience. It also minimizes errors and reduces the time needed to launch a project.


#4 Business Size
The number of employees in a UX/UI design agency determines how much effort it can put in a project or initiative. A large workforce is a good indicator of an agency’s success rate because it shows that it’s astute enough to invest in people and profitable enough to afford it. It also ensures that it has the professional experience and expertise to invest in your project. More people means more talent, and as higher level of proficiency that leads to better results.


#5 Portfolio, portfolio, portfolio
A UX/UI design agency is only as good as its portfolio. Before investing in one, you should request for a portfolio in your specific domain/vertical so you can see their past work and the philosophies behind them. It’s also a great idea to ask for a demo wherein the agency tells you about the journey from start to finish and how they can create a memorable experience for you and your users. Also ask the agency whether these past projects were completed up to spec and within the time frame provided.


#6 Soft Skills
Arguably the most important consideration when looking for a UX/UI agency, you should ensure that there’s effective communication at all times. Remember that contracting an agency means establishing a partnership that can make or break your project. As such, chemistry should be established at the onset so that there are little to no communication challenges for the duration of the project. This will also help with problem solving just in case there are setbacks along the way.


The UX/UI Bottomline


When strategizing, product design should be a major part of the process because it’s the number one success factor for your business. The customer is king—and a well designed product is the best way to make customers happy.


Design the best products by partnering with an established UX/UI design agency with demonstrated experience in your vertical and a solid portfolio of past successful projects. Keep communication lines open and make meaningful conversations to develop rapport and build a strong business relationship. A partnership built on trust and transparency will go a long way in ensuring product adoption and greater success.

Triolla's Mobile App UX Mastery Will Make Your App a Sensation


Find Out How to Create a Mobile App Users Can't Put Down with Triolla's UX Design Expertise


Mobile apps have become an essential part of our daily lives, from social media and entertainment to productivity and health. As mobile usage continues to grow, designing an effective and user-friendly mobile app is more important than ever. At Triolla, we have extensive experience in mobile app UX design, and we are here to share our expertise with you. In this article, we will explore the key bullet points to consider when designing a mobile app that provides an intuitive and engaging user experience.


![Musotic]


Focus on User-Centered DesignThe key to designing a successful mobile app is putting the user at the center of the design process. This includes understanding the user’s goals, motivations, and behaviors, as well as their expectations for the app. Conducting user research and usability testing can help ensure that the app meets the user’s needs and provides a seamless user experience.


![Musotic]


[contact-form-7 id=”958e338″ title=”Post Contact Form”]


Optimize for Mobile ContextMobile devices have unique characteristics that should be considered when designing a mobile app. These include small screen sizes, limited processing power, and varied network connectivity. Designing an app that is optimized for the mobile context can improve performance and usability. This includes minimizing load times, designing for touch-based interactions, and optimizing for different screen sizes and resolutions.


Develop a Clear Information Architecture and NavigationMobile apps often have complex functionality that can be challenging for users to navigate. A clear and intuitive information architecture and navigation can help users understand how the app works and how to interact with it. This includes designing clear and intuitive menus, buttons, and icons that guide the user through the app’s functionality.


![Musotic]


Implement Engaging Visual DesignVisual design is an essential component of mobile app UX, as it can impact the user’s emotional response and overall experience with the app. Implementing engaging visual design can improve user engagement and help the app stand out in a crowded marketplace. This includes using consistent branding, designing for a visually appealing layout, and incorporating animations and interactions that enhance the user experience.


At Triolla, we are committed to providing our clients with the highest quality mobile app UX design services. Our team of experienced designers and engineers has a deep understanding of the unique challenges and considerations that come with designing mobile apps. Contact us today to learn more about how we can help you create an effective and user-friendly mobile app that meets your business needs.

Unleash the Power of Your MVP to Accelerate Your Growth – UX Design for Startups


Uncover the Key Principles and Strategies for Designing an MVP That Captivates Your Target Audience and Boosts Your Startup’s Performance.


As a UX agency specializing in startup UX, we understand the importance of designing a successful MVP or prototype app or product. A well-designed MVP or prototype can make or break a startup’s success, and UX plays a critical role in that success. In this article, we will highlight the key bullet points to notice when designing a startup’s MVP or prototype.


Identify and Understand Your Target UsersOne of the essential factors in UX design is understanding your target users. Before starting to design your MVP or prototype, you need to identify your target audience and get to know their needs, expectations, and pain points. This information will help you design a product that meets the needs of your users, resulting in higher engagement and adoption rates.


Keep the MVP SimpleOne common mistake that startups make when designing their MVP is trying to cram too many features into it. Remember, the goal of the MVP is to validate your idea with minimal resources, time, and effort. Focus on developing the core features that solve the user’s pain points, and leave the nice-to-have features for later.


Focus on the User ExperienceThe user experience should be at the forefront of your design process. An excellent user experience means that your product is easy to use, intuitive, and enjoyable for your target audience. To achieve this, you need to design with the user in mind, which means taking into account their habits, preferences, and behaviors.


Design for Mobile FirstIn today’s digital age, mobile devices are the primary way people access the internet. As such, your MVP or prototype should be designed for mobile-first, with responsive design principles. This ensures that your product is accessible to a broader audience and delivers a seamless user experience across all devices.


[contact-form-7 id=”958e338″ title=”Post Contact Form”]


Test Early and OftenTesting is a critical step in the design process. Early testing allows you to validate your design assumptions and make changes before investing too much time and resources. Testing also helps you identify user pain points and opportunities for improvement. Regularly testing your MVP or prototype ensures that you’re creating a product that meets your user’s needs and expectations.


Implement AnalyticsAnalytics help you track user behavior, usage patterns, and other critical metrics. Implementing analytics from the start allows you to identify any issues or bottlenecks in your product’s flow and make necessary adjustments. Analytics also provide insights into what users like and don’t like about your product, which can help you refine your design and improve the user experience.


Be Consistent in Your DesignConsistency is key when designing a product. Ensure that all elements of your MVP or prototype are consistent, from the colors and typography to the layout and navigation. Consistency helps build trust and familiarity with your product, resulting in a better user experience.


Keep Your MVP or Prototype AgileAs a startup, your product is likely to evolve rapidly as you receive feedback and learn from your users. As such, it’s essential to keep your MVP or prototype agile, with the ability to adapt and iterate as necessary. This means designing a flexible product that can be easily modified and updated as you receive feedback.


ConclusionDesigning an MVP or prototype is a crucial step in the startup journey. A well-designed MVP or prototype can help validate your idea, attract investors, and acquire users. By keeping the user experience at the forefront of your design process, designing for mobile-first, testing regularly, implementing analytics, and keeping your product agile, you can ensure that your MVP or prototype is successful. At Triolla, we specialize in startup UX and can help you design a successful MVP or prototype. Contact us to learn more about our services.

The Essential Guide to Designing a Top – Performing Cyber App Mastering Cyber UX


Unleash the Full Potential of Your Cyber App with Key Insights and Strategies for User Experience, Security, and Accessibility.


As a UX agency specializing in cyber UX, we understand the critical role that UX plays in designing successful cyber apps and products. Cybersecurity is more critical than ever, and user experience can make or break a product’s security. In this article, we will highlight the key bullet points to notice when designing a cyber app or product.


Understand Your Users’ NeedsAs with any product or app, understanding your users’ needs is critical in designing a cyber app or product. In this case, it is especially important to consider the user’s level of technical expertise, knowledge of cybersecurity, and their security needs. Conduct user research to identify user needs, pain points, and behaviors to ensure that your design meets their expectations.


![ux for DeppKeep]


Prioritize SecuritySecurity is paramount in designing a cyber app or product. Consider the user’s data privacy and confidentiality, and ensure that your app or product meets the highest standards of cybersecurity. Work closely with security experts to ensure that your design incorporates the latest security protocols and best practices.


[contact-form-7 id=”958e338″ title=”Post Contact Form”]


Provide Clear and Concise InformationEffective communication is critical in cybersecurity. When designing your app or product, make sure that you provide clear and concise information about security risks, procedures, and best practices. Use simple language and visual aids to communicate complex concepts to users of all levels of technical expertise.


![ux for Armis]


Design for Ease of UseDesigning for ease of use is essential in cybersecurity. Users are more likely to follow security protocols when they are easy to use and understand. Design your app or product with an intuitive user interface, clear navigation, and simple workflows to help users complete security tasks with ease.


Use Feedback and AnalyticsUsing feedback and analytics is crucial in designing a cyber app or product. Analytics can help you understand how users interact with your product and identify areas for improvement. User feedback can also provide insights into user needs, pain points, and behaviors. Use both to continuously improve your design and meet user needs.


![ux for DeppKeep]


Design for AccessibilityDesigning for accessibility is critical in cybersecurity. Ensure that your app or product is accessible to users with disabilities, such as visual or hearing impairments. Consider the user’s needs when designing your app or product and provide alternative options for users who may not be able to use certain features.


Stay Up-to-Date with the Latest Cybersecurity TrendsStaying up-to-date with the latest cybersecurity trends is crucial in designing a cyber app or product. Cybersecurity is constantly evolving, and new threats and vulnerabilities are discovered every day. Stay current with the latest trends and best practices to ensure that your design incorporates the most effective cybersecurity measures.

Why Every Modern Company Needs a Stellar Dashboard UI – Insights from Triolla


We interact with them consistently. From morning check-ins to end-of-day reports, dashboards have become the unsung heroes in our professional lives, especially as the world leans into a hybrid working model post-pandemic. At Triolla, as leading UX designers serving Israeli startups and corporates, we believe in the potential of an expertly-crafted dashboard UI. Let’s delve into the art and science of creating an impeccable dashboard UI and understand how top brands nail it.


The Intriguing Origins of Dashboard UI


Ever pondered over the origins of the term ‘dashboard’? It harks back to the world of aviation and space. Pilots and astronauts rely on a control system, a ‘dashboard’ if you will, to navigate. But in a twist of nomenclature, it was the automotive sector that popularized the term. Traditionally, a dashboard referred to the panel indicating vital stats like speed, fuel, and temperature.


With the digital age in full swing by the early 2000s, the concept of a “Dashboard UI” emerged. In the world of UX UI portfolios, it represents a digital interface showcasing real-time Key Performance Indicators (KPIs). This is where decision-makers can gauge the pulse of their organization, thanks to this visually compelling data representation.


Mobile devices, novel design choices, and advanced data visualization like heat maps have since ushered in an era where dashboard UIs are more sophisticated and user-friendly.


Dashboard UI: More Than Just a Pretty Interface


Goal-Oriented Design is King


Despite evolving designs and trends, the core objective of dashboard UI design remains unaltered:


- Offer users a concise and clear snapshot of vital business metrics.

- Empower users with the data they need to make informed decisions efficiently.


By adhering to design conventions and best practices, designers at our UX studio and worldwide can craft dashboards that merge functionality with creativity. Think of it as an empowering tool steering your business towards its objectives.


[contact-form-7 id=”958e338″ title=”Post Contact Form”]


The Ubiquity of Modern Dashboard Designs


You might’ve noticed a striking similarity among modern dashboards, as if they’ve all been molded from the same UX UI portfolio blueprint. Why is that?


- Adherence to Standardization and Best PracticesOver the years, certain non-negotiable standards have been established for dashboard UIs. From lucid navigation and labeling to relevant data visualizations, designers leaning into these guidelines can inadvertently result in similar-looking UIs.

- Meeting User ExpectationsWith users now expecting specific features from their dashboards—like data drill-downs, custom views, and data filtering—designers work to integrate these elements. This user-centric design approach can sometimes result in UIs bearing a family resemblance.

- The Challenge of Design ConstraintsPresenting vast data amounts in a confined space is no easy feat. This often compels designers to embrace a minimalist design to aptly accommodate the data, which can again lead to similar UI aesthetics.

- Usability Trumps AllAt the heart of an effective dashboard UI is its ability to make data comprehension a breeze. Hence, designers often prioritize user-friendly features over aesthetic elements, leading to certain UI similarities.


However, it’s the nuanced touches that can set your dashboard UI apart. While the foundational structure might be standard, the play of branding elements, innovative typography, and colors can infuse uniqueness into your dashboard.


At Triolla, our expert UX designers prioritize crafting bespoke dashboard UIs that don’t just fit the mold but break it. After all, in a sea of similarities, it’s the unique touches that make a world of difference.

Navigating the Future of UX Design


Trends to Shape 2024 and Beyond.


The UX design landscape is continuously evolving, adapting to technological advancements and changing user needs. As Triolla look towards 2024 and beyond, several emerging trends are set to redefine the field of UX design. Drawing insights from leading sources like UX Collective, Forbes, Clutch, Nielsen Norman Group, and Toptal, this article explores the key trends that will shape the future of UX design.


The Rise of Conversational UX


One of the most significant trends is the rise of conversational UX. With the increasing integration of AI and machine learning, conversational interfaces like chatbots and voice assistants are becoming more sophisticated and user-friendly. UX Collective’s 2024 report highlights how these technologies are making digital interactions more natural and intuitive. Users now expect seamless, conversational experiences that mimic human interaction, pushing designers to create solutions that are not only functional but also engaging and empathetic.


The Focus on Ethical Design


Ethical design is another trend gaining momentum, as noted by Forbes in their 2024 insights. In an era where data privacy and user rights are paramount, UX designers are increasingly tasked with creating experiences that are not only effective but also ethical. This involves designing with privacy in mind, being transparent about data usage, and ensuring inclusivity and accessibility. Ethical design practices are becoming a cornerstone in building trust and loyalty among users.


The Growing Importance of Design Systems


Another trend set to dominate is the growing importance of design systems. As Clutch’s 2024 industry report indicates, design systems – a series of components and guidelines for designing applications and websites – are becoming vital for maintaining consistency and efficiency, especially for larger teams and complex projects. These systems enable designers to create cohesive user experiences across different platforms and devices, enhancing brand consistency and reducing development time.


[contact-form-7 id=”958e338″ title=”Post Contact Form”]


The Shift to a More Holistic Approach to UX


Nielsen Norman Group’s 2024 trends forecast a shift towards a more holistic approach to UX. This involves considering the entire user journey, rather than focusing on individual interactions or touchpoints. A holistic UX approach looks at the user’s overall experience with a product or service, taking into account their emotional, psychological, and behavioral responses. This trend signifies a move towards creating more meaningful and impactful user experiences that resonate on a deeper level.


The Increasing Use of Data and Analytics


Lastly, Toptal’s 2024 trends report emphasizes the increasing use of data and analytics in UX design. With vast amounts of user data available, designers can leverage analytics to gain deeper insights into user behavior, preferences, and pain points. This data-driven approach enables designers to create more personalized and effective user experiences. It’s about using data not just to inform design decisions but to anticipate user needs and tailor experiences accordingly.


Conclusion


As we advance into 2024, these emerging trends underscore a dynamic shift in the UX design industry. From conversational UX enhancing user interaction to the ethical responsibilities in design, from the efficiency of design systems to the depth of holistic approaches, and the power of data-driven design – these trends collectively represent a maturing field set to offer more nuanced and sophisticated user experiences. For UX professionals, staying abreast of these trends is key to creating innovative, user-centered designs that not only meet but exceed user expectations.


In summary, the future of UX design looks to be more intuitive, ethical, systematic, holistic, and data-informed. As these trends continue to evolve, they will undoubtedly bring new challenges and opportunities, shaping the way we think about and interact with the digital world.

Ahead of the Curve: Key UX/UI Developments to Watch in 2024


Trends to Shape 2024 and Beyond


Introduction
As we venture into 2024, the landscape of User Experience (UX) and User Interface (UI) design continues to evolve at a brisk pace. Staying abreast of the latest trends is not just about keeping up with technological advancements; it’s about understanding how these changes affect user expectations and interactions. This article delves into the most relevant and expected trends in UX/UI design for 2024, offering insights into how they will shape our digital experiences.


Personalization and Customization
One of the most significant trends in UX/UI is the shift towards personalization and customization. In an era where user attention is at a premium, delivering tailored experiences is key. Advanced algorithms and machine learning technologies are making it possible for designers to create interfaces that adapt to individual user preferences and behaviors. This means more intuitive navigation, customized content, and ultimately, a more engaging user experience. Businesses that harness these capabilities effectively will not only enhance user satisfaction but also see increased user engagement and loyalty.


Voice User Interface (VUI) and Conversational UI
The rise of voice assistants like Alexa and Google Home has ushered in a new era in user interface design. Voice User Interfaces (VUIs) and Conversational UIs are redefining how users interact with digital products. The challenge for UX/UI designers is to create voice interfaces that are both natural and efficient, catering to a wide range of user needs and contexts. As VUI becomes more prevalent, designers will need to consider voice interactions as integral to the user experience, ensuring they are seamless and intuitive.


Accessibility and Inclusive Design
Accessibility in UX/UI design is no longer an afterthought; it’s a necessity. Inclusive design ensures that digital products are usable by everyone, including people with disabilities. This trend is not only driven by ethical considerations but also by legal compliance. Designers are now prioritizing accessible design from the outset, ensuring that all users have equal access to information and functionality. This approach not only broadens the user base but also reflects a brand’s commitment to social responsibility.


[contact-form-7 id=”958e338″ title=”Post Contact Form”]


Augmented Reality (AR) and Virtual Reality (VR) in UX/UI
AR and VR technologies are transforming the UX/UI landscape. These technologies offer immersive experiences that were unimaginable a few years ago. From virtual try-ons in e-commerce to AR-based navigation apps, the applications are vast and varied. For UX/UI designers, this means exploring new paradigms of interaction where the physical and digital worlds converge. The challenge lies in designing experiences that are not only immersive but also intuitive and user-friendly.


Ethical Design and Data Privacy
In an age where data is king, ethical design and data privacy have become paramount. Users are increasingly aware of and concerned about how their data is used and stored. UX/UI designers must ensure that transparency and user consent are at the forefront of their design process. This involves designing interfaces that make it easy for users to understand what data is being collected and how it will be used, thereby building trust and ensuring a positive user experience.


Conclusion
The field of UX/UI design is at an exciting juncture, with emerging technologies and user expectations shaping its future. Staying updated with these trends is crucial for designers and businesses alike. By embracing personalization, voice and conversational interfaces, inclusive design, AR/VR technologies, and ethical design practices, designers can create experiences that are not only engaging and immersive but also respectful and inclusive. As we move forward, these trends will undoubtedly continue to evolve, setting new benchmarks for what constitutes an exceptional digital experience.

Behind the Wheel


Unveiling UX Design Challenges for Future Smart Dashboards


Introduction


The smart car dashboard represents the forefront of automotive innovation, blending advanced technology with user-focused design to transform how we interact with our vehicles. Yet, creating these sophisticated interfaces is far from straightforward. Designers and product managers alike are tackling a series of complex user experience (UX) challenges to ensure that these dashboards are not only feature-rich but also safe, user-friendly, and enjoyable for drivers of all backgrounds. From reducing driver distractions to achieving flawless integration with smartphones, the path to crafting the perfect smart car dashboard is fraught with obstacles demanding inventive solutions and a visionary approach. In this article, we explore the ten most pressing UXchallenges in smart car dashboard design, shedding light on the critical issues and exploring the potential for innovation in the automotive world.


What’s in the Market These Days?


As we delve into the realm of smart cars, the fusion of technology and automotive design has never been more apparent. Today’s market is teeming with examples of cutting-edge dashboard designs that push the boundaries of user experience (UX). From minimalist touchscreens to highly customizable digital instrument clusters, automakers are not just focusing on the aesthetics but also on how these interfaces enhance safety, efficiency, and personal connection with the vehicle. Innovations such as voice-controlled assistants, real-time adaptive displays, and seamless mobile integration are setting new standards. Let’s explore some standout examples from leading brands that exemplify the strides being made in smart car dashboard UX, showcasing how they tackle the complex challenges of today’s driving experience.


- Tesla Model S/X/3/Y: Tesla’s approach to dashboard design is minimalist and centered around a large touchscreen interface. This design choice emphasizes the challenge of minimizing driver distraction while providing intuitive access to a wide range of functionalities, from navigation to vehicle settings. Tesla’s software also continuously updates, showcasing how dashboards can evolve over time to meet new user needs and incorporate advanced technologies.

- Mercedes-Benz MBUX (Mercedes-Benz User Experience): The MBUX system stands out for its voice control capabilities, “Hey Mercedes” voice assistant, and the ability to learn from the driver’s habits. This addresses the challenge of integrating effective voice control and personalization into the car’s UX, offering a more intuitive and interactive experience.

- Audi Virtual Cockpit: Audi’s Virtual Cockpit is a fully digital instrument cluster that replaces traditional dials. It offers customizable information displays, integrating Google Earth imagery for navigation, and detailed car data. This innovation tackles the challenge of managing information overload by allowing drivers to tailor the dashboard display to their preferences and needs.

- Ford Mustang Mach-E SYNC 4A: Ford’s SYNC 4A system in the Mustang Mach-E features a large vertical touchscreen with cloud-connected navigation, voice recognition, and customizable profiles. It exemplifies the challenges of seamless mobile device integration and the importance of designing for contextual awareness, with features that adjust to driving habits and preferences.

- Volvo XC40 Recharge Google Android Interface: The Volvo XC40 Recharge incorporates an infotainment system powered by Google’s Android OS, offering Google Maps, Google Assistant, and access to the Google Play Store directly from the dashboard. This addresses the challenge of ensuring real-time performance and seamless integration with mobile devices and apps, setting a precedent for collaboration between automotive and technology companies.


[contact-form-7 id=”958e338″ title=”Post Contact Form”]


Designing UX for smart car dashboards presents a unique set of challenges that require careful consideration and innovative solutions. Here are ten UX challenges when designing for a smart car dashboard, highlighting the complexity and importance of user experience in the automotive industry:


- Minimizing Driver Distraction: The primary challenge is to design interfaces that provide necessary information and functionalities without diverting attention from the road. Balancing information accessibility with safety is crucial.

- Ensuring Accessibility for All Drivers: Dashboards must be universally accessible, catering to drivers of all ages and abilities. This includes considering visual, auditory, and physical impairments in the design process.

- Adapting to Diverse User Behaviors: Drivers have varied preferences and habits. Designing a dashboard that is intuitive for a wide range of users, from tech-savvy individuals to those less comfortable with technology, is a significant challenge.

- Integrating Voice Control Effectively: While voice control can reduce physical distractions, ensuring it works accurately under various conditions (like road noise or accents) is challenging. The system must understand and process commands efficiently to be truly beneficial.

- Managing Information Overload: Smart dashboards can display a vast amount of data, from navigation to vehicle status. Organizing this information without overwhelming the driver requires thoughtful UI/UX design strategies.

- Ensuring Real-Time Performance: Dashboard interfaces must operate in real-time, with minimal latency. Delays in displaying critical information (such as collision warnings) can compromise safety.

- Designing for Contextual Awareness: Smart dashboards should adapt to changing contexts, such as driving conditions, weather, and the driver’s state. Creating a system that intelligently adjusts what it displays based on context is complex.

- Balancing Personalization with Privacy: While personalization can enhance the driving experience, it raises privacy concerns. Designing a system that offers customization while safeguarding user data is a key challenge.

- Seamless Integration with Mobile Devices: Many drivers expect to connect their smartphones with their car dashboards. Designing an interface that integrates smoothly with a variety of devices and platforms is essential.

- Future-Proofing the Design: The automotive industry is rapidly evolving, especially with the advent of autonomous driving technologies. Designing a dashboard that can adapt to future advancements and remain relevant is a significant challenge.


As we navigate through the complexities of designing user experiences for smart car dashboards, it becomes evident that the journey is as intricate as it is innovative. Each challenge presents an opportunity to push the boundaries of what’s possible, blending technology with human-centric design to create safer, more intuitive, and engaging driving experiences. The future of automotive UX lies in our ability to adapt, innovate, and empathize with the end-user, ensuring that every advancement enhances the joy and safety of driving. As designers and product managers in this dynamic field, our mission extends beyond solving today’s challenges; it’s about anticipating the needs of tomorrow’s drivers and crafting experiences that make every journey memorable. In doing so, we are not just designing dashboards; we are reimagining the future of mobility itself. Let us embrace these challenges with open minds and creative hearts, driving forward to a future where technology and human experience merge on the road ahead.

Product-User Fit, Comes Before Product-Market Fit.


Product-user fit Vs product-market fit – Peter Lauten and David Ulevitch


Fascinating article from Andreessen Horowitz emphasizes that finding product-user fit is a critical precursor to achieving product-market fit for startups.
The full article: product market fit.


It distinguishes between product-user fit, where a product resonates deeply with a specific group of users, and product-market fit, where there’s a broader market demand.


[contact-form-7 id=”958e338″ title=”Post Contact Form”]


The piece highlights the importance of focusing on the needs and feedback of early power users to refine the product, which can lead to sustainable growth and eventually, product-market fit.


The authors argue that understanding and catering to these power users is key to unlocking a larger market opportunity.


Enjoy the article.

NLP & UX


Humanizing Digital Experiences One Word at a Time


Ever caught yourself thanking Siri, Alexa, or Google Assistant? There’s a reason why we sometimes forget we’re talking to a machine. It’s all thanks to Natural Language Processing (NLP) — a brilliant piece of technology that’s busy bridging the gap between human conversation and digital comprehension. This is where User Experience (UX) design teams up with NLP to craft interactions that feel less like pressing buttons and more like having a chat over coffee.


A New Era of Digital Interaction
In the realm of UX, NLP acts as a catalyst for innovation. Its mission? To make our dialogue with machines seamlessly intuitive. Imagine dictating an email to your laptop as if it were an attentive scribe, or querying a database with casual inquiries like you would ask a friend for recommendations. That’s the future we’re stepping into, where NLP stands as the cornerstone of user-friendly design.


Learning the Language of Design
Drawing inspiration from Kristina Hoogenboom’s insights on conversational design, it’s clear that communication is more than just words exchanged. It’s about context, timing, and emotion — factors that NLP and UX design strive to understand and implement. This synergy enables digital services to not just answer our queries, but to understand the intent behind them, making every interaction feel tailored and thoughtful.


The Ripple Effect of NLP on UX
The comprehensive review by Alessandro Russo and Michael Brauer opens up a fascinating dialogue on how NLP is reshaping user interfaces. From simplifying complex forms to offering personalized content, NLP-equipped UX design is setting a new standard for digital intuitiveness. It’s like having a personal guide within each app, one that speaks your language and anticipates your needs.


Real-World Magic of NLP in UX
Forbes and the Nielsen Norman Group shed light on practical examples where NLP enhances user engagement. Whether it’s through chatbots that handle customer service with ease or voice-activated systems that navigate users through websites hands-free, the impact is tangible. It’s transforming passive users into active participants, co-creating the digital experience with each command they voice.


[contact-form-7 id=”958e338″ title=”Post Contact Form”]


The Linguistic Labyrinth
However, integrating NLP into UX isn’t without its challenges. Language is a complex beast, filled with nuances, dialects, and slang. Designing systems that understand and adapt to this diversity requires not just technological prowess but a deep empathy for the end-user. It’s about ensuring that everyone, regardless of their language proficiency or cultural background, has equal access to technology.


Navigating the Future
As we look to the horizon, the fusion of NLP and UX design promises even more personalized, adaptive, and intuitive user experiences. Imagine interacting with applications that not only understand what you say but also how you feel, adjusting their responses accordingly. It’s a future where digital experiences are not just functional but truly meaningful.


A Glimpse into Chatbot UX
The literature review from Chatbots Magazine provides a case study in the art of chatbot design, highlighting the importance of personality, context-awareness, and user feedback in creating engaging conversational agents. It’s a testament to how far we’ve come and a hint at how much further we can go in making technology not just a tool, but a partner in our daily lives.


Humanizing Technology, One Interaction at a Time
So, what does all this mean for us, the users? It means that we’re moving towards a world where our interactions with technology are more natural, intuitive, and human. It’s about breaking down the barriers between humans and machines, making technology more accessible and enjoyable for everyone.


In Conclusion
The journey of integrating NLP within UX design is an ongoing adventure, filled with challenges, discoveries, and endless possibilities. As we continue to explore this synergy, one thing is clear: the future of digital interaction is not just about making technology smarter; it’s about making it more human.


 


FAQs


- ֿHow does NLP improve UX?
NLP enhances UX by making interactions with technology more natural and intuitive, allowing for a more personalized and efficient user experience.


 


- What challenges are there in combining NLP and UX?
The main challenges include handling the complexity of language, ensuring inclusivity across different languages and dialects, and maintaining privacy and security in user interactions.


 


- Can NLP truly personalize user experiences?
Yes, by analyzing and understanding user preferences and behaviors, NLP can tailor digital interactions to each individual, making experiences more relevant and engaging.


 


- What future trends should we look out for in NLP and UX?
Future trends include more advanced sentiment analysis, multi-modal interactions combining voice, text, and gestures, and even greater personalization through machine learning and AI.

UX|UI – FAQs


At Triolla, we believe that great UX design is about more than just aesthetics; it's about creating intuitive, seamless experiences that meet users' needs and exceed their expectations. There are many questions relating to UX and at Triolla we have most of the answers.


What is UX Design and why is it important?At Triolla, we believe that great UX design is about more than just aesthetics; it’s about creating intuitive, seamless experiences that meet users’ needs and exceed their expectations. Our UX design process involves thorough user research, detailed user personas, and iterative design testing to ensure that every interaction with your product is smooth and satisfying. By focusing on the user’s journey and identifying potential pain points, we craft designs that not only look good but also perform exceptionally well, enhancing user engagement and satisfaction.


What makes effective UI Design?The user interface (UI) design is a crucial component of any digital product, and at Triolla, we excel at creating visually stunning and highly functional interfaces. Our UI design process involves the use of modern design principles and tools to develop interfaces that are both attractive and easy to use. We pay close attention to every detail, from color schemes and typography to interactive elements, ensuring that the final product is not only beautiful but also intuitive. Our goal is to make sure that users can navigate your product effortlessly, resulting in a positive and memorable user experience.


How can Product UX Design accelerate growth?For products that are ready for a significant upgrade, Triolla offers specialized product UX design services. We work closely with your team to understand your vision and goals, conducting in-depth research and user analysis to inform our design decisions. Our approach ensures that your product not only meets but exceeds user expectations, driving growth and engagement. From initial concept to final implementation, our expert designers ensure that every aspect of the user experience is optimized for success, making your product stand out in the competitive market.


Why is UX Research essential for product success?Understanding your users is the foundation of successful UX design. Triolla conducts comprehensive UX research to uncover users’ hidden needs and motivations. Our research methods include user interviews, surveys, usability testing, and competitive analysis. By gathering detailed insights into how users interact with your product, we can identify areas for improvement and develop strategies to enhance the overall user experience. This user-centered approach ensures that the final product is both useful and delightful, meeting the real needs of your audience.


How does Digital Branding impact user experience?Digital branding is about creating a cohesive and compelling identity for your product that resonates with your target audience. At Triolla, we specialize in crafting digital branding strategies that encompass everything from logo design and color palettes to typography and imagery. Our goal is to create a strong, memorable brand that stands out in the digital landscape. By aligning your brand’s visual and verbal elements, we ensure that every interaction with your product reinforces your brand’s message and values, building trust and loyalty among your users.


What role does Front-End Development play in UX/UI design?The transition from design to a functional product requires skilled front-end development, and Triolla offers top-notch development services using the latest technologies like Vue, React, React Native, and Flutter. Our developers work closely with designers to bring the envisioned design to life, ensuring that the final product is not only visually appealing but also fast, responsive, and user-friendly. Whether you need a single developer or a full team, we provide the expertise needed to create high-quality digital products that perform seamlessly across all devices.

What is the importance of User Interface Design?Triolla excels in creating user interfaces that are both aesthetically pleasing and highly functional. Our user interface design process involves understanding the user’s needs, behaviors, and pain points to create interfaces that are intuitive and easy to navigate. We use modern design tools and methodologies to ensure that every element, from buttons to icons, contributes to a seamless user experience. By focusing on usability and accessibility, we create interfaces that users love to interact with, enhancing overall satisfaction and engagement.


How does Usability Testing improve user experience?Usability testing is a critical step in our design process at Triolla. It involves evaluating a product by testing it with real users to identify any usability issues and areas for improvement. Our usability testing methods include task analysis, heuristic evaluation, and user feedback sessions. By observing how users interact with your product, we can pinpoint specific problems and refine the design to make it more intuitive and user-friendly. This iterative process ensures that the final product meets the highest standards of usability and provides a superior user experience.


What is the process of Prototype Development?Developing a prototype is an essential part of the design process at Triolla. Prototypes allow us to test and refine ideas before full-scale development begins. Our prototypes range from simple wireframes to fully interactive models that simulate the final product. This approach enables stakeholders and users to provide valuable feedback early in the process, ensuring that the final design aligns with their needs and expectations. Prototyping helps us identify potential issues and make necessary adjustments, saving time and resources in the long run.


How is SaaS Platform Design approached?At Triolla, we specialize in designing SaaS platforms that are robust, scalable, and user-friendly. Our design process involves understanding the unique needs of SaaS users, such as ease of use, efficiency, and accessibility. We create interfaces that streamline workflows and enhance productivity, ensuring that users can achieve their goals quickly and efficiently. By incorporating best practices in UX and UI design, we develop SaaS platforms that not only meet but exceed user expectations, driving customer satisfaction and retention.


What professional UX Research services are available in Israel?Triolla offers professional UX research services in Israel, helping businesses uncover valuable insights about their users. By understanding user behaviors, needs, and pain points, we provide actionable recommendations that enhance the user experience. Our UX research services ensure that your product meets the real needs of your audience, leading to higher satisfaction and engagement.

F35 UX Vertigo


How the world's most advanced fighter jet's UX was designed and how it should be fixed.


Itay Racz , former WSO, Israeli Air Force.


No doubt the fifth-generation Lockheed Martin F-35 is an impressive machine. The cockpit, too, makes a striking first impression thanks to its touch screen interface, a first for combat aircraft. With a spatial full 360-degree display helmet one gets the feeling that this aircraft was built around humans, with user experience at the top of the considerations. Or was it?


As a former F 16 Fighter Falcon WSO and in my role leading the Israeli Air Force UX deparment I had very high expectations from the IAF newest addition – The F35 Lightning II. The airplance I used to fly, the F16, was designed in the 80’s. I couldn’t wait to see how far we have come with the most important point in any system – the connection (and pain) point between a human and a machine.


Lockheed Martin thought they figured it out. The logic was perfect – why ask UX “designers” to design a cockpit when you can ask pilots. The pilots that were asked were veterans, experienced pilots. What could possibly go wrong? Just about everything. “DESIGNED BY PILOTS FOR PILOTS” makes as much sense as “cooked by diners for diners”. Pilots know how to fly a plane, the way they are used to fly a plane. They don’t know a better way, they don’t know what don’t they know. Additionally, the TTM of an airborne tech is measured in decades. The pilots gave it their best about 20 years ago. UX has come a long way since, and today’s pilots were raised by iPhones. They don’t know and don’t care how things were in the past.


Main Displays:


The cockpit features large touch screens that have replaced the gauges, buttons, and switches of previous generations. However, these are “TOUCH” screens rather than “MULTI-TOUCH” screens. Unlike the multi-touch screens we use daily on our phones, these touch screens offer limited gestures and inputs (such as zooming with two fingers or swiping), increasing the pilot’s cognitive load.


Information Arrangement in the PCD (Pilot Combat Display)


The scattered arrangement of buttons is a holdover from older screens where buttons (OSBs) were placed around the screen. Those were “soft buttons” that change their function according to the changing label next to it. It worked quite well at the time but the F35 solution – leave the arrangement and change the input method basically takes the worst of the two worlds – it doesn’t use the old method clarity and tactile feedback and doesn’t use the touch screen’s main advantage – WYSIWYG (What you see is what you get). Additionally, with touch screens our eyes scan the screen—top to bottom, then left to right, just like in a book. New pilots are not used to look for things around the screen and this layout cannot support logical hierarchy and flow within the screen.


HMD (Helmet Mounted Display):


The 360-degree view using six cameras around the plane is a remarkable feature but has a significant drawback. The lack of static objects, such as the plane’s wing or body, which would typically interfere with the world view, affects spatial orientation. The pilot expect to see a wing when he looks to his side. He can look at the wing and orient himself according to its movement relative to the background. If a pilot see a moon rises over the tip of the right wing he knows the wing is dipping, and he’s probably turning right. When there is no wing, there’s no way to judge the aircraft speed and orientation relative the background. This is expecially vital in bad weather,  and night missions.


[contact-form-7 id=”958e338″ title=”Post Contact Form”]


HUD (Head-Up Display)


The HUD in the F35 is virtual. There’s no piece of glass mounted on top of the dashboard. Instead it’s presented by the helmet, but only when looking forward. When looking sideways, there’s no clear and easy way to know the plane’s pitch and roll.


Knobs, handles, levers:


Traditional knobs and handles were designed to have exceptional tactile feedback. So much so that they are designed to look like their function. The landing gear lever is shaped like a landing gear, including the wheel. The flaps handles are flat, the engine throttle is round. All these were replaced with purely digital functions. An extreme examples is the refueling port hatch.


Midair refueling is a critical mission and a dangerous one. The pilot has to manage a mid air collision safely, the process requires a series of actions that need to be done in time and on time. The very last thing that the pilot needs to do is open the refueling port hatch.


This should be done quickly, as late as possible so a dedicated lever was designed to look like a flat hatch so it’s easy to find and operate under a stressful refueling manouver. In the F35 there isn’t a physical hatch latch anymore. The process now requires three clicks on 3 different areas of the touch screen.


After Action Review:


The sleek design of the F-35 cockpit falls short of expectations due to a lack of understanding of modern digital displays and user experience principles. The attempt to mimic physical levers and handles on screen didn’t work, and on the other hand, a lot of old habits were applied to the new architecture, whereas the same technology could have allowed for a much easier, streamlined operation. In the air, in an expensive machine flying hundreds of miles an hour, UX is crucial and needs to be rethought and redesigned on the F35 Lightening II.


#uxdesign #userexperience #humanengineering #aviationtechnology


#uxfail

UX is Life, design it for humans.


The digital products we interact with should feel as natural as opening a door. You shouldn't need a manual to figure out how to send a message, make a payment, or navigate a website. If a design requires instructions, the design isn’t intuitive enough. Great UX design feels like an extension of life—it’s easy, logical, and fits our expectations of how things should work. UX is life, design it for humans.


Every door that needs a PUSH or PULL sign is a design fail. Good UX needs no expanation. In fact there’s a name for this kind of door, or more accurately there’s a name for this kind of UX – Norman door. Named after cognitive scientist Don Noram, Norman doors are doors that operate differently than what the reasonable user would assume. Don Norman brought attention to the frustration users feel when design conflicts with intuition. A Norman Door, in essence, operates opposite to what a reasonable person might expect, and it points to a deeper issue in the world of design: when things are difficult to use, they fail us. UX is life, design is for humans.


[](https://www.amazon.com/Design-Everyday-Things-Revised-Expanded/dp/0465050654)A textbook for designers, a must book for Product Managers


Micael Caine once said that if someone complements his acting it means he failed his job. Acting shouldn’t be noticed. What’s important is the actual experience, not the meta. The beauty of design lies in its ability to be invisible—when done right, you hardly notice it’s there. Good design is an extension of how we naturally interact with the world. The closer it mimics the logic and expectations of human behavior, the more effortless it feels. When you walk through a properly designed door, you don’t stop to think. You simply know how to use it. No instructions are needed, no frustration arises. It just works, seamlessly, intuitively.


The same applies to UX design. The digital products we interact with should feel as natural as opening a door. You shouldn’t need a manual to figure out how to send a message, make a payment, or navigate a website. If a design requires instructions, the design isn’t intuitive enough. Great UX design feels like an extension of life—it’s easy, logical, and fits our expectations of how things should work.


[contact-form-7 id=”958e338″ title=”Post Contact Form”]


[](https://www.pitangoux.com/projects/)It’s about trust. You trust a door with a handle to be swing open when you pull on it. If it doesn’t, you don’t know if it’s a Norman door or maybe the venue is closed. A friend of mine developed a whatsapp bot for finding help in the neighborhood. The bot was a bit slow, but this tiny delay had no feedback of any sort, and caused numerous users to quit the app thinking it was malfunctioning. Others clicked again and again to no avail. Creative Panda here explains what’s up. Transparency and clarity bring confidence and trust, and help people relax with the clicking.


It’s about trust. You trust a door with a handle to be swing open when you pull on it. If it doesn’t, you don’t know if it’s a Norman door or maybe the venue is closed. A friend of mine developed a whatsapp bot for finding help in the neighborhood. The bot was a bit slow, but this tiny delay had no feedback of any sort, and caused numerous users to quit the app thinking it was malfunctioning. Others clicked again and again to no avail. Creative Panda here explains what’s up. Transparency and clarity bring confidence and trust, and help people relax with the clicking.


Think about the objects you love using in your everyday life. Maybe it’s your favorite app, the tap-to-pay feature on your phone, or a streaming service that just “gets” what you want to watch. These experiences stand out because they are thoughtfully designed to anticipate your needs. They don’t force you to adapt to them; instead, they adapt to you, making the interaction pleasant, seamless, and even joyful.


But professionals deserve joy too. The more complicated the system, the more challenging the UX. Onboarding should be quick, time is money, and if a system can’t integrate quickly into what people know and do, people would choose not use.


Now, compare this to frustrating experiences—like poorly designed forms that ask redundant questions, or clunky systems where you’re forced to click through endless steps to achieve a simple goal. In these moments, you feel the weight of bad design. It interrupts your flow, wastes your time, and creates unnecessary friction between you and your goal.


[](https://www.pitangoux.com/projects/)Professionals deserve joy too. And the more complicated the system, the more challenging the UX. Onboarding should be quick, time is money, and if a system can’t integrate quickly into what people know and do, people would choose not use.


Good design smooths out the rough edges between humans and technology, allowing the two to coexist in harmony. A well-designed product respects the user’s time, their attention, and their mental effort. It doesn’t demand more of them than necessary. This is where UX design becomes more than just a functional aspect of a product—it becomes an essential part of how we experience life. As we said, UX is life, design is for humans.


The best UX design is invisible, just like the best tools are those that feel like natural extensions of our bodies. A hammer, a pencil, a phone—all of these tools are made great when they don’t get in the way. The same principle applies to digital design. UX design is about reducing pain points, removing obstacles, and creating joy in how we interact with the world around us.


Ultimately, good UX is good life design. The interactions we have with technology, whether physical or digital, shape our daily experiences. When UX is thoughtful, it elevates these experiences from frustration to ease, from confusion to clarity, from stress to joy.


So, the next time you use a product that feels natural, intuitive, and effortless, take a moment to appreciate the design behind it. Because in the end, UX is life. It’s the bridge between humans and the technology that powers our lives, and when that bridge is built with care, it leads to a better, more connected world. UX is life, Design it for humans


#UXislife
#UXUIdesign

Whether you’re looking for a full fledged UX UI agency or an inhouse team of designers, Triolla is your go-to partner for creating world-class digital experiences.


We understand the unique challenges businesses face in a competitive digital landscape. That’s why Triolla stands out as a UX studio dedicated to quality over quantity. Our boutique approach means we work closely with each client, offering a collaborative experience that ensures your vision comes to life. 7 Emerging UI/UX Design Trends Every Development Team Should Be Aware Of


In the dynamic world of technology, the importance of UX (User Experience) is paramount. The role isn’t merely about design aesthetics; it revolves around creating an engaging and intuitive user experience.


 


As technology progresses, so does the arsenal of tools and techniques at the disposal of UX designers. Staying ahead of the curve, at Triolla, we’ve been pioneering the art of blending emerging trends with core design principles, catering especially to the vibrant Israeli startup and corporate scenes. However, with technological evolution comes a change in user expectations. Their exposure to new technological paradigms shifts their preferences. Any tech enthusiast, whether a budding startup or a well-established corporate, must be aware of these changing dynamics. It’s essential not only for crafting the best user interfaces but also for carving a standout UX UI portfolio.


1. Embracing Design Systems in UX Studios
The concept of a design system might have once been overlooked, but in today’s UX-driven age, it’s indispensable. Platforms like Figma and Sketch are enabling UX designers to manage reusable components efficiently, resulting in faster design processes and more synchronized collaboration. Design systems, once just a component of a UX UI portfolio, now stand as a testament to a brand’s design maturity.


2. Prioritizing Inclusive Design
Inclusion isn’t just a trend; it’s a necessity. A significant stride in product design, inclusive design underscores the importance of crafting products usable by everyone, regardless of their abilities or experiences. For us at Triolla, inclusivity isn’t just a point in our UX UI portfolio; it’s a principle we embed into every design.


---


3. Illuminating the Benefits of Dark Mode
Dark mode isn’t just a passing fad. With its eye-friendly, energy-efficient traits, it’s rapidly becoming a must-have feature in UX design. At Triolla, we understand the growing preference for this feature. Incorporating dark mode isn’t just about following a trend; it’s about recognizing and implementing what enhances user comfort in our UX studio projects.


---


4. The Power of Simplicity
One can’t stress enough the beauty of simplicity. As UX designers, we’ve often been faced with the challenge of simplifying interfaces without compromising functionality. At Triolla, the question isn’t “how much can we add?” but rather “how simply can we convey the essence?”. A minimalist yet impactful UX UI portfolio often speaks louder than a cluttered one.


[contact-form-7 id=”958e338″ title=”Post Contact Form”]


---


5. Engaging Conversations: The Rise of Conversational Interfaces
With the release of powerful tools like ChatGPT, conversational interfaces are changing the game. These interfaces, powered by sophisticated AI, are paving the way for more intuitive user interactions. In our UX studio at Triolla, we’re always exploring how to weave in this technology, ensuring our clients remain at the forefront of innovative user engagement.


---


6. Empowering Users: The Need for End-User Input
Today’s user is not just a passive consumer. They seek to have a voice in how applications function. Recognizing this, we at Triolla actively promote the inclusion of end-user input in our design strategies. A well-crafted UX UI portfolio is as much about user feedback as it is about designer innovation.


---


7. Revolutionizing Text Input and Output with LLM
While touch interfaces dominate the current era, the resurgence of text input, particularly powered by Large Language Models (LLM), is undeniable. Be it through typing or voice recognition, this old-school interaction method is getting a futuristic makeover. Our UX designers are keenly exploring how to incorporate this into our dynamic design strategies.


---


In a rapidly evolving digital landscape, staying ahead of trends is crucial for any development team. From the rise of dark mode to the increasing importance of micro-interactions, these seven UI/UX design trends are shaping the future of how we interact with digital products. By understanding and implementing these trends, development teams can create more engaging, user-friendly, and innovative digital experiences. As technology continues to advance, staying informed and adaptable will be key to success in the ever-changing world of UI/UX design.


---

Radio Button – Episode 122 From Freelancer to a Successful Bussiness


, "”": You Conquer One Mountain Only To See The Next One Ahead” When Asaf started working as a freelancer, he did not plan on building a large company. His goal was simple: to do what he loved, which was helping companies improve their user experience.


Design had always fascinated him, and he believed in the power of visual language. However, he quickly realized that freelancing was not just about doing great work. It also required managing himself, attracting clients, and turning small projects into real business opportunities.


Facing Challenges and Growing Step by Step


The journey was not easy. Asaf recalls the early days when he faced challenges on his own. He had to find clients, set prices, negotiate deals, and prove the value of thoughtful design. At a pivotal moment, his brother Yuval joined him. Together, they began to think strategically about how to grow their work into something bigger.


Step by step, their efforts started to pay off. Projects grew in size, clients returned, and they rented office space. Soon, they were hiring employees. Despite their progress, they always kept one thing in mind: every mountain they conquered revealed another one ahead.


Turning Expertise into a Business


In a recent podcast episode, Asaf and Adi discuss this critical turning point. They explore how to transform expertise in a specific field into a stable and growing business. For Asaf, this transition required a major mindset shift. He was no longer just a design expert. He had to become a businessman, a team manager, and a partner to his brother.


Success, they realized, was not just about the quality of their work. It depended on creating a system that worked. Clients needed to understand why they should choose them. Processes had to be clear, from sales to service delivery. They invested in branding, built a team, and developed a methodology that helped them grow from a small service company into a significant player in the field.
[contact-form-7 id=”958e338″ title=”Post Contact Form”]


Overcoming Common Challenges


The conversation also touches on the challenges they faced along the way. How do you price your work correctly? How do you convince companies to invest in you over competitors, especially when results are not always immediate? How do you attract big clients when you are still perceived as a freelancer?


One key lesson Asaf learned was to stop chasing projects and start building processes that brought clients to them. He and Yuval adopted a more organized approach. They created clear price quotes, structured sales processes, and a professional business language. These changes helped them appear as a reliable and established company.


Building a Brand That Lasts


Adi raises an important point in the episode about building a brand. She emphasizes that building a brand is about more than just numbers. Successful companies thrive not only because of the services they provide but also because of the reputation they create.


In the early years, Asaf and Yuval invested heavily in networking, attending events, and doing everything it took to build a name in the market. These efforts laid the foundation for their long-term success.


The Takeaway: Think Big, Start Small


By the end of the conversation, one thing becomes clear. Transitioning from freelancer to business owner does not happen overnight. It takes courage, flexibility, and a commitment to thinking big. Asaf and Yuval started with small steps, but their consistent investment allowed them to grow from a two-brother company into a leading brand.


For product managers and entrepreneurs, the key takeaway is this: business success is not just about talent or expertise. It is about creating the right processes and thinking ahead. That is what turns good work into a thriving business.


Listen to the Full Episode


A big thank you to Adi Levin for the opportunity to share Asaf and Yuval’s story. You can listen to the full episode here: Spotify link.
