Triolla's Mobile App UX Mastery Will Make Your App a Sensation


Find Out How to Create a Mobile App Users Can't Put Down with Triolla's UX Design Expertise


Mobile apps have become an essential part of our daily lives, from social media and entertainment to productivity and health. As mobile usage continues to grow, designing an effective and user-friendly mobile app is more important than ever. At Triolla, we have extensive experience in mobile app UX design, and we are here to share our expertise with you. In this article, we will explore the key bullet points to consider when designing a mobile app that provides an intuitive and engaging user experience.


![Musotic]


Focus on User-Centered DesignThe key to designing a successful mobile app is putting the user at the center of the design process. This includes understanding the user’s goals, motivations, and behaviors, as well as their expectations for the app. Conducting user research and usability testing can help ensure that the app meets the user’s needs and provides a seamless user experience.


![Musotic]


[contact-form-7 id=”958e338″ title=”Post Contact Form”]


Optimize for Mobile ContextMobile devices have unique characteristics that should be considered when designing a mobile app. These include small screen sizes, limited processing power, and varied network connectivity. Designing an app that is optimized for the mobile context can improve performance and usability. This includes minimizing load times, designing for touch-based interactions, and optimizing for different screen sizes and resolutions.


Develop a Clear Information Architecture and NavigationMobile apps often have complex functionality that can be challenging for users to navigate. A clear and intuitive information architecture and navigation can help users understand how the app works and how to interact with it. This includes designing clear and intuitive menus, buttons, and icons that guide the user through the app’s functionality.


![Musotic]


Implement Engaging Visual DesignVisual design is an essential component of mobile app UX, as it can impact the user’s emotional response and overall experience with the app. Implementing engaging visual design can improve user engagement and help the app stand out in a crowded marketplace. This includes using consistent branding, designing for a visually appealing layout, and incorporating animations and interactions that enhance the user experience.


At Triolla, we are committed to providing our clients with the highest quality mobile app UX design services. Our team of experienced designers and engineers has a deep understanding of the unique challenges and considerations that come with designing mobile apps. Contact us today to learn more about how we can help you create an effective and user-friendly mobile app that meets your business needs.

Navigating the Future of UX Design


Trends to Shape 2024 and Beyond.


The UX design landscape is continuously evolving, adapting to technological advancements and changing user needs. As Triolla look towards 2024 and beyond, several emerging trends are set to redefine the field of UX design. Drawing insights from leading sources like UX Collective, Forbes, Clutch, Nielsen Norman Group, and Toptal, this article explores the key trends that will shape the future of UX design.


The Rise of Conversational UX


One of the most significant trends is the rise of conversational UX. With the increasing integration of AI and machine learning, conversational interfaces like chatbots and voice assistants are becoming more sophisticated and user-friendly. UX Collective’s 2024 report highlights how these technologies are making digital interactions more natural and intuitive. Users now expect seamless, conversational experiences that mimic human interaction, pushing designers to create solutions that are not only functional but also engaging and empathetic.


The Focus on Ethical Design


Ethical design is another trend gaining momentum, as noted by Forbes in their 2024 insights. In an era where data privacy and user rights are paramount, UX designers are increasingly tasked with creating experiences that are not only effective but also ethical. This involves designing with privacy in mind, being transparent about data usage, and ensuring inclusivity and accessibility. Ethical design practices are becoming a cornerstone in building trust and loyalty among users.


The Growing Importance of Design Systems


Another trend set to dominate is the growing importance of design systems. As Clutch’s 2024 industry report indicates, design systems – a series of components and guidelines for designing applications and websites – are becoming vital for maintaining consistency and efficiency, especially for larger teams and complex projects. These systems enable designers to create cohesive user experiences across different platforms and devices, enhancing brand consistency and reducing development time.


[contact-form-7 id=”958e338″ title=”Post Contact Form”]


The Shift to a More Holistic Approach to UX


Nielsen Norman Group’s 2024 trends forecast a shift towards a more holistic approach to UX. This involves considering the entire user journey, rather than focusing on individual interactions or touchpoints. A holistic UX approach looks at the user’s overall experience with a product or service, taking into account their emotional, psychological, and behavioral responses. This trend signifies a move towards creating more meaningful and impactful user experiences that resonate on a deeper level.


The Increasing Use of Data and Analytics


Lastly, Toptal’s 2024 trends report emphasizes the increasing use of data and analytics in UX design. With vast amounts of user data available, designers can leverage analytics to gain deeper insights into user behavior, preferences, and pain points. This data-driven approach enables designers to create more personalized and effective user experiences. It’s about using data not just to inform design decisions but to anticipate user needs and tailor experiences accordingly.


Conclusion


As we advance into 2024, these emerging trends underscore a dynamic shift in the UX design industry. From conversational UX enhancing user interaction to the ethical responsibilities in design, from the efficiency of design systems to the depth of holistic approaches, and the power of data-driven design – these trends collectively represent a maturing field set to offer more nuanced and sophisticated user experiences. For UX professionals, staying abreast of these trends is key to creating innovative, user-centered designs that not only meet but exceed user expectations.


In summary, the future of UX design looks to be more intuitive, ethical, systematic, holistic, and data-informed. As these trends continue to evolve, they will undoubtedly bring new challenges and opportunities, shaping the way we think about and interact with the digital world.

The 3 Most Common Pain Points when Hiring UI/UX Agency for a SAAS Product


The process of hiring for any role can be taxing and expensive regardless of the nature of work you do. It might seem like a simple task at first, but it requires a significant investment of company resources. Aside from the time and money you need to spend to find the best people for the job, you also need the manpower with the necessary skills that will help you find the right fit.


It’s the same case when it comes to choosing the right UI/UX agency. To help you address the challenges surrounding this endeavor, below are the top 3 pain points you should consider when hiring UI/UX agency.


- Short on resourcesThe process of hiring in-house UI/UX designers can put a lot of weight on a company’s resources, especially if the process drags on. It’s not always easy to find the people with the specific skillset that you need, so the process takes time. If your company is short on resources, financial or otherwise, this process can be cause for concern.

- Difficulty finding experienced UI/UX designersOne of the main reasons for this is supply—it’s limited and most of what’s left is being recruited by larger companies. Often, startups and smaller companies are left with no choice but to work with less experienced designers or agencies. A LinkedIn report has shown that UX design is one of five skills that are most in demand since 2020.

- Difficulty finding UI/UX designers with an industry specific experienceIt’s hard enough to find experienced UI/UX designers; it’s even harder to find ones that have a background on the certain niche you’re working in. When selecting the agency or people to work with, you should ensure that you meet eye to eye when it comes to goals and expectations.


Triolla: A UI/UX Agency With Vast SAAS Experience


Brilliant ideas are excellent starting points for new products, but UI/UX requires more than that. This is where a UI/UX agency like Triolla comes in. Triolla’s vast experience in the software as a service space takes excellent product ideas and brings them to life with a design principle based on specific client requirements and current market trends.


With Triolla as your UI/UX agency partner, you can experience success for the entire process until your product is live in production.


Here are some points you should consider when evaluating a UI/UX agency:


 


AvailabilityYour chosen UI/UX design agency should always be within reach in case there are issues that need to be addressed or modifications that need to be made on a project. This ensures quick turnaround times and avoids miscommunication that can be the cause of significant delays and other setbacks. Triolla can also start immediately on your project so you can get your product to market quicker and more efficiently.


Relevant experienceThe Triolla team comprises a team of experienced UX/UI designers, with extensive backgrounds in a variety of applications, systems, and platforms, and product UX experts, with proven track records in the field of product characterization and design. With 10 years of industry experience, Triolla knows the market and can create buyer personas appropriate to your industry. The company has worked on projects in the eCommerce, gaming, tourism, transportation, high technology, and mobile industries.


Easy scalabilityTriolla projects are designed to be scalable because it follows the “accordion effect.“ When a client wants to expand, the project structure is decentralized; in case of an economic downturn, it scales down to a centralized structure. The typical UI/UX flow is within 3–4 months, after which work is limited to the addition of new features and tweaking of existing ones. This puts less load on overhead and helps minimize overall cost.


[contact-form-7 id=”958e338″ title=”Post Contact Form”]


Cost effectivenessBecause hiring a senior designer or a number of junior designers is more expensive than the cost of a 3-month project, Triolla presents a more feasible solution without sacrificing quality of work and set deadlines. The core of product design, especially in the field of software and SaaS, is minimizing risk by working with someone or a team who has done it hundreds of times while working with the most competitive companies in the space.


“No I in team”Rather than hiring an individual, it’s always better to hire an experienced team of designers so there are more ideas on the table and there are always people to consult. More experienced people working on a project means it will take less time to complete because of a more efficient workflow. A team also ensures that there’s someone overseeing the project as it progresses, so issues are easily addressed and alternative solutions are presented.


Only the best of the bestTriolla prides itself with an excellent team that’s dedicated to their craft—and the clients. The company and its team of expert UI/UX designers has extensive experience working with both up-and-coming startups and established global companies, including Nike, Playtica, Lufthansa, and more. Triolla is the go-to company for SaaS system, AI system, and intra-organizational platform design.


Experience Success is Triolla’s Mission


Ultimately, it all boils down to experiencing success. For Triolla, that experience is leveraged to provide a standard of excellence that satisfies clients and ensures the success of every project. If a client saves millions in product UI/UX design and makes a successful product launch, then the company’s mission has been accomplished.


Triolla’s extensive experience in the SAAS space has made the company an expert in leading customer experience satisfaction by applying the right design by the right experienced people.


A human-centered approach puts the focus on the users and on providing the most seamless experience possible while also addressing common digital challenges and pain points. The professional collaboration between product and UI/UX experts also brings about innovative ideas that lead to high-value products and memorable user experiences.


Many companies start with a great idea but fail in execution because they don’t have a specific and cohesive product in mind. This is where Triolla becomes the missing piece in the product design puzzle. By designing a system and product that’s tailored to fit the specific needs of its clients, Triolla ensures an efficient go-to-market (GTM) strategy and a shorter time to bring the product to market.

Six Things You Need to Check Before Hiring a UX/UI Agency


Choosing a UX/UI design agency presents its own challenges because it's a core component of your product and how you want your customers to experience it. When it comes to the product, the customer is still king.


Choosing a UX/UI design agency presents its own challenges because it’s a core component of your product success. The customer is king when it comes to product adoption and engagement, and this is the arena where you should win your battles. The pandemic has pushed forward drastic changes in customer behavior, and the “stickiness” of these changes will depend largely on customer satisfaction. As such, one of your business goals should be creating a product that would provide a seamless and intuitive experience to your users.


This is where UX and UI design come in.


Each concept is complex in itself; combined, they can be a source of frustration even for those who understand the core concepts of user experience and user interface. Building an engaging product or mobile application that’s also well optimized can be very challenging, but hiring a UX/UI design agency ensures that your application is, aside from being aesthetically pleasing, quick and easy to browse, reliable, and rich with features that improve the overall user experience.


Finding the Right UX/UI Design Agency for Your Business


To ensure that your design philosophy conforms to your business goals, you should find an agency that understands your business inside out. This means that you yourself should have a deep understanding of your business and what it stands for, including how you want it presented to prospects and customers. The aesthetics, functionality, and ease of use of your product is your best tool for making a good first impression and attracting the right audience. Ensure that it represents your business, its value proposition, and how this is offered to your customers through its content and overall design and structure.


It’s best to create a list of must-haves and things to consider before working with a UX/UI design agency to help you identify salient points and things you need to discuss with potential providers. Below is a list of things to consider before you jump into a partnership with an agency.


[contact-form-7 id=”958e338″ title=”Post Contact Form”]


#1 Agency Proficiency 
If you’re working on a product, it’s only logical to find a UX/UI design agency that specializes in products. A product-oriented company with vast experience will deliver value that goes beyond your expectations. It also aligns both your expectations when it comes to project constraints. Most project parameters will obviously be dependent on the product, so a product focus will definitely prove beneficial for both parties.


#2 Availability
Availability is an important factor because your timelines will be largely dependent on how available and flexible your UX/UI design agency is. Not everybody is available to start a new project immediately and give it the attention you require. However, the details should be clear at the onset so the agency knows what needs to be done and when it should be completed. The agency should be able to provide an estimate of when a project will be completed.


#3 Vertical Expertise
If you’re looking for a personalized touch, you should look for a UX/UI design agency that has significant experience in your specific vertical. This ensures that it has a deeper understanding of your business, what it does, and the markets it serves. An agency that demonstrates real experience in your domain can provide a personalized touch peppered with relevant expertise and experience. It also minimizes errors and reduces the time needed to launch a project.


#4 Business Size
The number of employees in a UX/UI design agency determines how much effort it can put in a project or initiative. A large workforce is a good indicator of an agency’s success rate because it shows that it’s astute enough to invest in people and profitable enough to afford it. It also ensures that it has the professional experience and expertise to invest in your project. More people means more talent, and as higher level of proficiency that leads to better results.


#5 Portfolio, portfolio, portfolio
A UX/UI design agency is only as good as its portfolio. Before investing in one, you should request for a portfolio in your specific domain/vertical so you can see their past work and the philosophies behind them. It’s also a great idea to ask for a demo wherein the agency tells you about the journey from start to finish and how they can create a memorable experience for you and your users. Also ask the agency whether these past projects were completed up to spec and within the time frame provided.


#6 Soft Skills
Arguably the most important consideration when looking for a UX/UI agency, you should ensure that there’s effective communication at all times. Remember that contracting an agency means establishing a partnership that can make or break your project. As such, chemistry should be established at the onset so that there are little to no communication challenges for the duration of the project. This will also help with problem solving just in case there are setbacks along the way.


The UX/UI Bottomline


When strategizing, product design should be a major part of the process because it’s the number one success factor for your business. The customer is king—and a well designed product is the best way to make customers happy.


Design the best products by partnering with an established UX/UI design agency with demonstrated experience in your vertical and a solid portfolio of past successful projects. Keep communication lines open and make meaningful conversations to develop rapport and build a strong business relationship. A partnership built on trust and transparency will go a long way in ensuring product adoption and greater success.

NLP & UX


Humanizing Digital Experiences One Word at a Time


Ever caught yourself thanking Siri, Alexa, or Google Assistant? There’s a reason why we sometimes forget we’re talking to a machine. It’s all thanks to Natural Language Processing (NLP) — a brilliant piece of technology that’s busy bridging the gap between human conversation and digital comprehension. This is where User Experience (UX) design teams up with NLP to craft interactions that feel less like pressing buttons and more like having a chat over coffee.


A New Era of Digital Interaction
In the realm of UX, NLP acts as a catalyst for innovation. Its mission? To make our dialogue with machines seamlessly intuitive. Imagine dictating an email to your laptop as if it were an attentive scribe, or querying a database with casual inquiries like you would ask a friend for recommendations. That’s the future we’re stepping into, where NLP stands as the cornerstone of user-friendly design.


Learning the Language of Design
Drawing inspiration from Kristina Hoogenboom’s insights on conversational design, it’s clear that communication is more than just words exchanged. It’s about context, timing, and emotion — factors that NLP and UX design strive to understand and implement. This synergy enables digital services to not just answer our queries, but to understand the intent behind them, making every interaction feel tailored and thoughtful.


The Ripple Effect of NLP on UX
The comprehensive review by Alessandro Russo and Michael Brauer opens up a fascinating dialogue on how NLP is reshaping user interfaces. From simplifying complex forms to offering personalized content, NLP-equipped UX design is setting a new standard for digital intuitiveness. It’s like having a personal guide within each app, one that speaks your language and anticipates your needs.


Real-World Magic of NLP in UX
Forbes and the Nielsen Norman Group shed light on practical examples where NLP enhances user engagement. Whether it’s through chatbots that handle customer service with ease or voice-activated systems that navigate users through websites hands-free, the impact is tangible. It’s transforming passive users into active participants, co-creating the digital experience with each command they voice.


[contact-form-7 id=”958e338″ title=”Post Contact Form”]


The Linguistic Labyrinth
However, integrating NLP into UX isn’t without its challenges. Language is a complex beast, filled with nuances, dialects, and slang. Designing systems that understand and adapt to this diversity requires not just technological prowess but a deep empathy for the end-user. It’s about ensuring that everyone, regardless of their language proficiency or cultural background, has equal access to technology.


Navigating the Future
As we look to the horizon, the fusion of NLP and UX design promises even more personalized, adaptive, and intuitive user experiences. Imagine interacting with applications that not only understand what you say but also how you feel, adjusting their responses accordingly. It’s a future where digital experiences are not just functional but truly meaningful.


A Glimpse into Chatbot UX
The literature review from Chatbots Magazine provides a case study in the art of chatbot design, highlighting the importance of personality, context-awareness, and user feedback in creating engaging conversational agents. It’s a testament to how far we’ve come and a hint at how much further we can go in making technology not just a tool, but a partner in our daily lives.


Humanizing Technology, One Interaction at a Time
So, what does all this mean for us, the users? It means that we’re moving towards a world where our interactions with technology are more natural, intuitive, and human. It’s about breaking down the barriers between humans and machines, making technology more accessible and enjoyable for everyone.


In Conclusion
The journey of integrating NLP within UX design is an ongoing adventure, filled with challenges, discoveries, and endless possibilities. As we continue to explore this synergy, one thing is clear: the future of digital interaction is not just about making technology smarter; it’s about making it more human.


 


FAQs


- ֿHow does NLP improve UX?
NLP enhances UX by making interactions with technology more natural and intuitive, allowing for a more personalized and efficient user experience.


 


- What challenges are there in combining NLP and UX?
The main challenges include handling the complexity of language, ensuring inclusivity across different languages and dialects, and maintaining privacy and security in user interactions.


 


- Can NLP truly personalize user experiences?
Yes, by analyzing and understanding user preferences and behaviors, NLP can tailor digital interactions to each individual, making experiences more relevant and engaging.


 


- What future trends should we look out for in NLP and UX?
Future trends include more advanced sentiment analysis, multi-modal interactions combining voice, text, and gestures, and even greater personalization through machine learning and AI.

Classical Conditioning and User Experience


By Aya Nisan, UX/UI Designer at Triolla.


The definition of classical conditioning in English is a term coined by Ivan Pavlov, a Russian physiologist, and physiologist who in 1888 conducted a series of experiments that dealt with the digestive system of dogs. He tested digestive and gastric fluids in dogs, more specifically he noticed that dogs salivate at the sight and smell of food, but beyond that, he began to understand that whenever they see him, they start to associate his face with food and automatically salivate, so he actually wanted to see how it could be connected other food stimulus to get the same saliva response.


So what exactly is Pavlov’s rule of thumb? A bit of terminology – Pavlov presented the dogs with the unconditioned stimulus that causes a reflexive physiological response and always, an unconditioned response was formed. The unconditioned response is strongly biological to the dog and is involuntary. The experiment was that each time he presented the food, he rang a bell and repeated the action several times. The conditioned stimulus is neutral, a bell should not cause any dog to salivate. After repetition of this action, learning took place for the dog, and they started salivating even when they simply heard the bell.


This conditioning is the most basic axiom for learning. It is found almost everywhere if you think about it – almost every action we do is based on classical conditioning.


So what does it have to do with user experience?


Using USABILITY, we can take an existing condition that has already been created in our brain and rely on it, if that means colors, motivation for action, and certain symbols that have already been given to us in our brain a long time ago. Let’s take, for example, the color green as symbolizing something positive or normal. We use existing conditions and would not like to create new conditions not to bother the user.


[contact-form-7 id=”958e338″ title=”Post Contact Form”]


ENGAGEMENT involvement to condition a new action – think about a voluntary response we would like to receive from the client, such as joy, fear, retention, and motivation to use. We can use the conditioning of a conditioned stimulus for an unconditioned stimulus we can produce this conditioning. We will take the basic human need to belong, to be part of a group, to succeed in relation to others as a kind of social comparison.


For example, the need to belong can be from the never-ending refreshing of the feed, the feedback I receive from an app, they will like my photo, I will see how many people viewed my profile on LinkedIn and how many compared to last week’s. If I wrote a funny post on a social network so the number of followers would increase by a few more, it would make me happy. Thus I would have the condition that every time I read my feed, I would be motivated to get a feeling of happiness.


Another example is the feeling of dopamine – a slight feeling of happiness released in the brain when I succeed in a task and feel good about myself. This is a condition that exists beautifully in social networks and all interfaces on the Internet. We want to produce small moments of happiness and raise the level of engagement among our users. This can be done by allowing the user to increase their level of use, such as the number of followers and the number of recipes they have finished uploading, and causing the user to accumulate some kind of process he has done within the interface.


To combine gamification and a leaderboard – where I stand in my progress in the interface in relation to surfers and customers similar to me, it is important for me to know who is the best or who excelled when I am in the top five, I will be satisfied with my progress.


Allow users to follow other users – visually show the status of users vis-a-vis other users, create social influence, and interact between users. If I now receive a comment on my post and I like this post, I tell another user I liked the comment, it was effective, and that’s how we feed each other. These examples create better UX for our users.

PMs – Own your Product Design Process with these simple steps


The product design process requires complex interpersonal skills. The Triolla team presents some tips for properly managing the process.


What are the best practices for creating and maintaining positive and efficient organizational culture? How to complete your tasks without getting into a beef with your counterparts daily? How to successfully manage the workflow while overcoming differences and disagreements?If you are a Product Manager working closely with UX\UI designers, these are definitely some of the questions you are often asking yourself.


Creating an outstanding product is a meticulous process that demands teamwork, collaboration, and multi-disciplinary symbiosis. As a product manager, you will have to navigate the workflow facing numerous challenges to achieve the final goal.


As many PM professionals point out, healthy personal relationships with your counterparts, particularly the design team, are essential. In this article, our Triolla experts will share their take on the best PM-designer collaboration practices. They will provide key recommendations for building a sustainable and healthy organizational culture.


We are partners!


Treat the designers fairly, and include them early. Treat the UX designers on your team as partners, not as assistants. This mindset of teammates striving to accomplish a certain goal should lead you as a Product Manager right from the start.


Include the designers in the process as early as possible. Invite them to participate at the beginning of the UX mapping, and the customer needs decision-making process. Respect their insights and professional recommendations. The earlier your designers are involved in the process, the fewer setbacks and frustration your team will experience.


Make them feel valued and appreciated. Encourage them to share their vision, opinions, and concerns openly. Then effectively integrate the designers into the work process to secure high motivation and a mutual desire to succeed.


Let’s communicate


Open, personal and positive communication is essential to your success. Emphasize open, transparent, and direct talks with your partners. Invest time in developing genuine friendships and mutual understanding. Learn your designer’s perspective, terms, language, and thought process. Constantly maintain a proactive and responsive approach. Solve any conflict or disagreement at the earliest stage and never let it escalate and flare. Embrace the compromise while minding the key milestones that define success.


Although it might sound obvious, it is not. A lack of constructive and positive communication usually disrupts any work process and might lead to unnecessary tension and conflicts in your team. Therefore, it might be a good idea to choose a more humble approach and to get rid of any ego as soon as possible. Sustain these core guidelines during the entire work process, and we are confident you will accomplish your target with flying colors.


Lead with an outcome-oriented mindset


Your teammates and partners look up to you, don’t let them down. As a PM, you are directly responsible for the success (or the failure) of a particular project, a client, or a whole UX portfolio. It doesn’t mean that the burden is solely yours to carry, yet you must establish an outcome-oriented mindset in your team to promote smooth, efficient, and constant progress.


Set clear goals and expectations. Define responsibilities and timelines.Create an alignment in your multi-disciplinary team by setting clear objectives and key results. Make sure that these objectives and results are measurable and feasible. Specify mutual success milestones and, by all means, avoid micromanagement.


Treating your partners as valued professionals (who they are) will gain their cooperation and respect, reduce tension and ensure an overall positive working experience.


[contact-form-7 id=”958e338″ title=”Post Contact Form”]


When reality knocks on your door


Don’t let emotions get on your path to success. The PM-Designer relationship is not different from any other relationship. Disagreements are essential components of any work process, and the right thing to do is to harness them to improve the outcome.As the Product Manager, you should embrace the compromise. Stay focused on the goal while balancing creativity, risks, budget, etc.


Even during times of differences with your teammates, keep it professional, never personal. Maintain a rational mindset and keep the emotions away.


Avoid these mistakes


Here are the successful Product Manager commandments you should copy/paste:


- Micromanagement – is a “creativity killer.”You need the designers on your team to be creative and open-minded. Trust your partners and let them do their jobs.

- Set a clear success path – It’s impossible to keep your team motivated and dedicated when they partially understand the project. Ensure that the whole picture is clear and everyone is on board.

- Neglecting or avoiding personal relationships – We can’t stress it enough! The personal relationships created on your team will define the success or the failure of a given task.


If you made it here, you are certainly on the right path. You must already be aware of the complexity and intensity of your position as a product manager, yet you are up for the challenge. These are some core principles kindly provided by our Triolla experts, and we strongly encourage you to follow their guidance.


This is a part of our Triolla San Francisco and UX California updates; sign up for our newsletter to get biweekly updates.

How to sync with your product designer – Pro's best practices


The Triolla team of experts has compiled the ultimate software toolbox of the world’s most popular tools for product managers. If you are a product manager or UX\UI designer, you will find this article particularly helpful.


Whether you are relatively new to product management or a seasoned PM, this article is necessary for professional development and growth.


The first three on our list are comprehensive task management tools that, in our opinion, are a “must-have” in any product manager’s toolbox. Monday / Clickup and Jira are setting their standards in our industry, and both platforms are essential for efficient team and task management.


Monday.com


Online product management platform Monday.com allows teams of any size to plan, track, and manage their daily work. Whether it’s large-scope product roadmaps or weekly iterations, Monday.com enables teams to define clear ownership, track and analyze their work, manage sprints, and collaborate. With Monday.com’s agile platform, teams can collaborate from anywhere, regardless of their physical location.


You can create any agile workflow your team needs with Monday’s operating system’s visual and flexible features.


Clickup


Clickup is a cloud-based project management software that allows you to manage projects while offering numerous features and ensuring they are affordable and straightforward. Teams can collaborate and define shared tasks, complete with status updates and project updates, to align workflows with objectives. Due to its high degree of customization and ability to provide excellent visibility into each project and job, we consider it one of the best project management software solutions available.


Jira


Atlassian’s Jira is proprietary software for issue tracking, bug tracking, and agile project management. First released in 2002, Jira is gaining popularity and has been used by over 180,000 customers across 190 countries. It is compatible with multiple languages on macOS, Windows, and Linux, and It also has a mobile app version for Android and iOS devices.


Jira offers four main subscription plans: Jira Work Management, Jira Service Management, Jira Align, and Jira Software. Jira Work Management is a project management tool. Jira Service Management is for IT operations, and Jira Align is for product and portfolio management. Tracking bugs and issues were Jira Software’s original purpose, yet It has evolved into a powerful help desk management, task management, product management, and agile project management tool. Jira is also a great test management tool for software development.


Next on our list are two roadmapping and strategy alignment tools that will keep you on the right track. Getting your product on a focused, efficient path is where product roadmapping tools come in.


ProductPlan


ProductPlan is a roadmapping and collaboration tool in one.


In addition to creating and sharing unlimited roadmaps, you can pivot between timeline, list, and table views. An extensive template library comes in handy when you don’t want to start from scratch, and the drag-and-drop editor makes it easy to modify your roadmap as you go on.


A “comments and mentions” function is a great addition allowing you to communicate with your teammates directly on the platform.


Building your roadmap based on dates, having a broad “portfolio view” in one click, and tons of different roadmap-sharing options make Productplan one of our favorites. Oh.. and you can integrate with JIRA, Pivotal Tracker, Team Services, and Slack.


Productboard


Another product management tool used for creating roadmaps, prioritizing features, and collecting user feedback is Productboard.


The roadmaping feature is particularly impressive, allowing you to prioritize and group all your product-related features and even tailor your roadmap according to the audience. Productboard can easily integrate Jira, Slack, and Amplitude for a seamless workflow.


Productboard’s core feature is user feedback, and in our opinion, this is a “dealbreaker.” In addition to increasing customer satisfaction, Productboard allows you to aggregate product insights and customer requirements across multiple inboxes, including Slack. Productboard will interest you if you need a continuous feedback loop for your products.


[contact-form-7 id=”958e338″ title=”Post Contact Form”]


When it comes to gathering and analyzing user behavior data, our experts got you covered with these two special software that we are constantly using:


Fullstory


FullStory is a web-based digital intelligence system that helps optimize the client’s experience and provides a comprehensive glance into the customer’s journey. It enables our experts to track and monitor each customer’s activity. Everything is automatically indexed, and all the indexed information is accessible to the entire team, including click maps, page transitions, and layouts. Fullstory software collects data that assists our team in understanding how future users interact with the technology and guide business decisions. FullStory users have access to powerful features allowing them to conduct quantitative and qualitative analysis simultaneously. Combining these features with Session Replay provides clarity and context around user behavior, from a bird’s eye view to individual user sessions.


Lastly, when it comes to design and prototyping, our Triolla professionals picked two distinguished winners:


Figma


Figma is a cloud-based design tool that can be used for practically anything! Besides designing, you can also prototype interactions, animate transitions, add multiple artboards, animate vectors with timeline-based animations, add live previews while editing, and publish your changes.


One of Figma’s most desirable features is live commenting and feedback from your counterparts to get real-time collaboration on the go.


Figma is the only browser-based software that runs on any OS, avoiding the infamous Mac-IOS clash. It can be easily integrated with Slack and other project management tools. Because it is cloud-based, sharing and updating have always been challenging. Overall, Figma got a solid spot on our favorites list.


Miro


Miro is a digital whiteboard that makes collaboration easy. You can create notes and designs using the software, move things around, and communicate through video conferences or online chats. Additionally, the tool provides several pre-built templates that can serve as inspiration or a starting point for your project work. We often use Miro at our remote brainstorming and design sessions.


With Miro you can conveniently:


- Create and share any list of ideas or topics

- Build a user story or customer journey map

- Engage your team during a brainstorming session or a workshop

- Wireframe a new product concept or idea

- Lay out a roadmap or strategy for an innovation workshop or program


Miro can easily integrate with other team managing and collaboration tools such as Google Drive, Slack, Asana, Trello, and SurveyMonkey.


Zeplin


Zeplin bridges the gap between designers and engineers with a desktop plugin and standalone application for Windows and Mac. It takes designs from Sketch, Adobe XD CC, Figma, or Adobe Photoshop CC and exports them into a format that generates code snippets, design specs, and assets. Zeplin produces CSS code for every component used in the design.


It is an excellent tool for mockups and prototyping and allows several users’ real-time collaboration.


Invision


InVision Freehand is a cloud-based digital product design platform that helps us create and manage prototypes. Users can collaborate, test, and experiment with designing templates and ideas on a digital dashboard. InVision features include presentations, prototypes, digital whiteboards, wireframes, planning, and feedback management. A user’s workflows and prototype development can be streamlined and automated using the Inspect module. Vector editing, layer styling, and animated drawings are available in InVision’s Studio tool. A shared design library helps professionals collaborate on instant playback, mirroring mobile devices, and editing timelines.


Product managers must have access to various product management tools to deliver products that satisfy customers’ needs. Having the right tools in your stash ensures optimal workflows, smooth collaboration, and a data-driven approach to building products your users will love.


These tools often improve your product management operations, and adding a new tool to your arsenal can do wonders for productivity, communication, and results.


We hope the tool list our experts at Triolla kindly provided includes the one tool you’re looking for, helping you improve team communication and work efficiency. This is a part of our Triolla San Francisco and UX California updates; sign up for our newsletter to get biweekly updates.

The ultimate product design process; The best practice used by Google, Facebook, Netflix, etc


In this article, we share our product design methodology. This simple yet highly effective approach allows us at Triolla to constantly provide our clients with outstanding products and remarkable results.


Onboarding – allocating the right people for the job


Our process begins with the onboarding phase as we define together with our client his needs and the process’s goals. What kind of products does he want to design, and on what schedule? Aligning these expectations helps us match the dedicated work team to the client’s specific domain. At this stage, the client acknowledges that the professionals who will work with him are experts in his industry; these people are dedicated and experienced.


We believe in accumulated knowledge & experience at Triolla. Therefore allocating a full team that will manage the project includes researchers, UX consultants and UI designers, and a senior UX professional to overview and supervise the process.


 


Discovery


A workshop of several hours is conducted during the discovery stage for all stakeholders to brainstorm all project elements. After this session, all the team members will gather a clear vision and understanding of the various aspects of the future product. Example of questions asked during the kickoff meeting:


- What is the purpose of a particular product or feature?

- What is the need or an issue that it is supposed to address?

- What is the expected demand, and who is the audience?

- Are we improving an existing product or creating a new one?


These are just some of the questions answering which we will be able to promptly and efficiently determine the most suitable strategy for your case. Identifying the client’s “pain points” is another important aspect of asking these questions. These are the underlying causes of the setback. Whether it is a lack of professional skills, budget limitations, or time, we need to have a clear vision of the value we can provide to our client.


Market research


We learn and take inspiration from our direct and indirect competitors. Often our competitors face the same challenges as we are, while conducting a competitive analysis may provide us with necessary insights regarding design patterns, specific industry standards, and different approaches to the same issue. We want to learn from and get inspired by industry standards and opinion leaders’ products.


Providing our services to diverse portfolios and industries over the years is one of our significant advantages as a large-scale UX agency. As our experts analyze different verticals (industries with shared characteristics such as Gaming, Fintech, Medical, etc.), they can easily adjust a particular solution applied in one case to address an issue at a completely different vertical. The assortment of portfolios, flexible thinking, and accumulated experience are one of Triolla’s primary assets.


Another element of the research is the investigating & defining User Persona. We are looking for the most profound perception of who is the user of the product and how does its user journey look like right now. Before we make any conclusions, our multidisciplinary team of experts must identify the goals and motivations of future users and their expectations of the product. That can be done using several tools, including interviews, surveys, contextual inquiries, etc. Wisely applying these tools will help us formulate reliable representations of the critical audience segments when empathizing with our users.


Moreover, “Heatmap analyses,” for instance, provide us with essential data to assess the different aspects of user behavior while using our product. We will later apply this data to the ideation and execution phases.


[contact-form-7 id=”958e338″ title=”Post Contact Form”]


User flow and Data Architecture


This is a web platform, app, or product structure. Using this tool, such as a UX canvas, users can understand where they are and where the information they need is relative to their current position. A navigation system, hierarchical structure, and categorization system are created as part of the IA building process. Information architecture, for instance, refers to designing a blueprint that helps users better understand where they are on a website. The user experience will also be impacted by how we arrange our product’s features, functions, and available data.


Visualizing user’s journey


The ideal user experience and interaction with the future product are graphically described in this step. It provides a holistic user experience vision, ensuring its consistency and fluidity. In addition, the user journey also serves as the basis for defining the product specifications and requirements. The customer/user journey can differ from product to product, but most user journeys have three phases: Onboarding/registration, First time experience, and daily use/retention.


Wireframing


This is when the future product’s skeleton is created. Our team will create a visual guide representing the structure, the hierarchy, the interactions, and the critical elements of the product. This is also an excellent opportunity to address and tackle upcoming challenges and ideas with team members and stakeholders to ensure interface usability and reduce design time by baselining the core information architecture.


Graphical Concept – defining the user experience


By this point, we have a clear concept of what we must do to successfully design the product, our strategy, and how to prioritize. The design team is ready to start building the product now that they know what needs to be done. You, as the client, will review our progress and choose the desirable wireframe to proceed with.


Concept Meeting: Setting the baseline for designing the graphic interface, including color palette, fonts, images, input fields, and buttons. This step ensures visual consistency throughout the application by establishing a baseline for the various graphic interface elements.


User Interface Design: UI Design


Once the graphical concept is chosen, the style guide is applied based on the wireframes to create the end-looking screens. GUIs provide the final aspect of the product’s screens to our client for approval before implementation.


Prototype


The best way to experience the product before we develop it is to create a Prototype.The prototype will allow all stakeholders of the product to examine & evaluate it from different perspectives. Often, prototypes begin with a few core parts (usually crucial user flow) and expand as necessary over multiple iterations until all required areas have been covered. Prototyping facilitates feedback collection from stakeholders, potential users, and investors.


Product managers and entrepreneurs also use this tool as a fundraising tool and in front of other stakeholders to familiarize them with the usability of the tool or application.


Usability Test


This is a more formal process we use with some of our clients; We take the various screens to potential customers and people from within the company and show them the prototype to identify whether the product can be used efficiently and entirely as we researched. We can draw many conclusions from this stage on success indicators such as dwell times, percentage of abandoning the product, etc.


Handover to R&D


It is time to release the design to the R&D for its final iteration. Again, the designer will provide detailed specifications describing precisely what needs to be done.At this stage, we transfer the prototype to development. This is critical for completing the process, and communication is crucial here. We involve the customer here to facilitate the final development process of the product. Sometimes, we add a final stage of Design QA, during which the original design is examined and compared to the final development to check that no elements were left out during the product’s development phase.


A prototype handoff doesn’t mean the job is done and the product design process is over. On the contrary, testing and designing should be an ongoing, repetitive process.


I greatly recommend Triolla as the first choice for your next business endeavor. Our vast experience working with multiple industries, our outstanding team of professionals, and our uncompromising standards for product design and user experience optimization will bring you the desired success!


The product design methodology we shared with you is a proven path for planning & designing complex platforms and apps. Follow those steps and experience success. This is our product design methodology – a complete and efficient way to give the client the best product possible. This is a part of our Triolla San Francisco and UX California updates; sign up for our newsletter to get biweekly updates.

Enhancing Customer Satisfaction Through Positive User Experience and User Delight


Have you ever wondered why some products have a special place in our hearts and we keep coming back to them again and again? The answer lies in their positive user experience that brings joy and satisfaction to the users. And, at Triolla, we believe that taking this experience to the next level through “User Delight” can be a game-changer for any product. In this blog post, we will delve into what User Delight is and how it can help organizations create exceptional experiences for their users. Join us on this exciting journey as we explore the power of positive user experience with User Delight. By Shanee Beattie, UX/UI Designer at Triolla


User Delight is a concept that adds a positive emotional touch to a user’s digital experience, be it on a website, app or any other interface. Achieving User Delight involves a combination of functional and usable design, as well as adding a pleasurable touch to the overall user experience.


To understand the concept of User Delight better, it can be divided into two parts: surface delight and functional delight. Surface delight includes micro-animations, videography, and other interactive elements that are visually engaging and add a fun element to the user experience. On the other hand, functional delight is all about reducing pain points, making the experience as smooth and user-friendly as possible.


[contact-form-7 id=”958e338″ title=”Post Contact Form”]


There are three main reasons why User Delight is important. Firstly, a positive emotional experience will lead to a passionate and returning user, who is more likely to recommend the product to others. This will increase the popularity of the product and ultimately lead to a better return on investment for the client. Secondly, anticipating the user’s needs and tailoring the experience to their preferences will create a more personalized experience and make the user feel valued. Finally, incorporating unique and creative elements such as artwork, voice recognition, or transitions between pages, can help to differentiate the product from others and make it stand out.


Some examples of brands that have successfully incorporated User Delight into their products include Netflix, with its endless scroll of possibilities, TikTok, with its personalized onboarding process, and Lemonade, an insurance company that uses humor and fun animations to engage users and encourage them to sign up.


In conclusion, incorporating User Delight into the user experience design process is crucial for creating an emotionally engaging and memorable experience for users. By focusing on functional and surface delight and making the user the center of the experience, companies can differentiate their products and create a loyal user base.


This is a part of our Triolla San Francisco and UX California updates; sign up for our newsletter to get biweekly updates.

Revolutionizing Healthcare with UX Design


Transform the Healthcare Industry with These Expert UX Tips for Health App Design.


6 Key Tips for Designing Winning Medical Apps


The healthcare industry is rapidly evolving, and with it comes an increased demand for digital products and services that can improve patient outcomes and healthcare efficiency. At Triolla, we understand the unique challenges of designing for healthcare, and we have extensive experience in creating user-centered designs for medical professionals, patients, and caregivers. In this article, we will share some key points to keep in mind when designing a health app or product, based on our expertise in medical UX design.


User ResearchThe key to creating an effective health app is to understand the needs and behaviors of your target audience. Conducting user research can provide valuable insights into the preferences, pain points, and goals of your users. For example, you may discover that patients prefer apps that provide educational content or tracking tools to help manage their conditions. On the other hand, medical professionals may prioritize apps that save time and improve communication with patients. By conducting user research early in the design process, you can ensure that your app meets the needs of your target audience.


![medical ux digitalowl]


medical ux digitalowl


AccessibilityHealthcare apps must be designed with accessibility in mind to ensure that they can be used by people with disabilities or impairments. This includes making sure that the app is compatible with screen readers and other assistive technologies, as well as designing for color blindness and other visual impairments. By prioritizing accessibility in your design, you can ensure that your app is inclusive and can be used by the widest possible audience.


UsabilityHealth apps must be easy to use and navigate, especially for patients who may be dealing with complex medical conditions. This means designing a clear and intuitive interface, with logical navigation and labeling. It is also important to ensure that the app is easy to learn, with clear instructions and onboarding processes. By prioritizing usability in your design, you can create an app that is accessible and effective for a wide range of users.


![medical ux digitalowl]


medical ux digitalowl


Data SecurityHealthcare apps must comply with strict data security regulations to protect sensitive patient information. This includes using encryption, secure login procedures, and data backup and recovery systems. It is also important to ensure that your app is HIPAA compliant if it is dealing with medical records or other patient data. By prioritizing data security in your design, you can build trust with your users and ensure that their information is kept safe.


[contact-form-7 id=”958e338″ title=”Post Contact Form”]


Integration with Healthcare SystemsHealthcare apps must be designed to integrate seamlessly with existing healthcare systems, such as electronic health records (EHRs) and other clinical systems. This can improve communication between medical professionals and patients, as well as streamline administrative tasks. It is important to ensure that your app is compatible with these systems and that it can be easily integrated into existing workflows. By prioritizing integration in your design, you can create an app that improves healthcare efficiency and outcomes.


User FeedbackHealth apps must be designed to evolve over time based on user feedback and data. This means building in feedback mechanisms, such as user surveys or in-app analytics, to collect data on user behavior and preferences. It also means being responsive to user feedback and making updates and improvements based on that feedback. By prioritizing user feedback in your design, you can create an app that is constantly improving and meeting the changing needs of your users.


In conclusion, designing a health app or product requires a deep understanding of user needs, healthcare regulations, and technical requirements. By prioritizing user research, accessibility, usability, data security, integration, and user feedback, you can create an app that meets the unique needs of the healthcare industry. At our UX agency, Triolla, we have extensive experience in medical UX design and can help you create a digital product that improves patient outcomes and healthcare efficiency. Contact us today to learn more about our services and capabilities.

Level Up Your Gaming App with Triolla's Expert UX Tips – Boost User Engagement and Retention


Discover the Key Considerations for Designing an Engaging and Effective Gaming App with Triolla’s UX Strategies.


At Triolla, we have extensive experience in designing user-centered experiences for a wide range of industries, including gaming UX design. In this article, we will focus on the key considerations when designing a gaming app or product with a user experience (UX) approach. Whether you are creating a game for entertainment, education, or other purposes, these tips will help you design an engaging and effective user experience.


![Spring Games]


Spring Games


User ResearchThe first step in creating a successful gaming app is to understand your target audience and their needs. User research can provide valuable insights into the preferences, behaviors, and pain points of your users. For example, you may discover that your users prefer games with challenging levels or educational content. By conducting user research early in the design process, you can ensure that your game meets the needs of your target audience.


Onboarding and TutorialsIt is important to provide clear and concise onboarding and tutorial processes for your game. This can help users understand the mechanics and rules of the game and reduce the learning curve. By designing an intuitive and engaging tutorial, you can improve the user experience and increase user retention.


![ux for fox baby]


ux for fox baby


Navigation and Menu DesignNavigation and menu design are critical components of a successful gaming app. It is important to design clear and intuitive menus that allow users to easily access game features and information. This includes designing clear icons and labels, as well as logical grouping of features. By prioritizing navigation and menu design in your game, you can create a seamless and engaging user experience.


Game Mechanics and BalancingThe game mechanics and balancing play a key role in the success of a gaming app. It is important to design a game with balanced difficulty levels and a clear progression system. This can help users feel challenged but not overwhelmed, which can improve engagement and retention. By testing and iterating on game mechanics and balancing, you can create a game that is enjoyable and addictive.


[contact-form-7 id=”958e338″ title=”Post Contact Form”]


Visual Design and GraphicsThe visual design and graphics of a game can have a significant impact on the user experience. It is important to design a game with a consistent visual style and theme that is engaging and visually appealing. This includes designing clear and easy-to-understand visual cues, as well as high-quality graphics and animations. By prioritizing visual design and graphics in your game, you can create a memorable and immersive experience for your users.


![madskill]


madskill


User Feedback and AnalyticsUser feedback and analytics can provide valuable insights into user behavior and preferences. It is important to build in feedback mechanisms, such as user surveys or in-app analytics, to collect data on user behavior and preferences. This can help you understand how users are interacting with your game and identify areas for improvement. By prioritizing user feedback and analytics in your design, you can create a game that is constantly improving and meeting the changing needs of your users.


In conclusion, designing a successful gaming app requires a deep understanding of user needs, game mechanics, and technical requirements. By prioritizing user research, onboarding and tutorials, navigation and menu design, game mechanics and balancing, visual design and graphics, and user feedback and analytics, you can create a game that is engaging and effective. At Triolla, we have extensive experience in designing user-centered gaming experiences and can help you create a game that stands out in the crowded gaming market. Contact us today to learn more about our services and capabilities.

Designing an Engaging and Effective Agritech App


Grow Your Agricultural Business with Triolla's Tips.


Discover the Key Considerations for Creating an Intuitive and Effective Agritech App with Triolla’s Expert UX StrategiesAt Triolla, we specialize in creating user-centered experiences for a diverse range of industries, including healthcare, gaming, and agriculture. In this article, we will focus on the key considerations for agritech product design. Whether you are creating an app for precision farming, agricultural supply chain management, or other purposes, these tips will help you design an intuitive and effective user experience.


User ResearchThe first step in creating a successful agritech app is to understand your target audience and their needs. User research can provide valuable insights into the preferences, behaviors, and pain points of your users. For example, you may discover that your users prefer apps that provide real-time updates on weather patterns or crop yields. By conducting user research early in the design process, you can ensure that your app meets the needs of your target audience.


![PitangoUX UX/UI Design Agritask]


Triolla UX/UI Design Agritask


Data VisualizationThe agricultural industry generates vast amounts of data, from crop yield reports to weather patterns. It is important to design a user interface that can effectively visualize this data in a clear and actionable way. This includes designing clear and intuitive graphs, charts, and maps that allow users to quickly and easily understand data trends and patterns.


[contact-form-7 id=”958e338″ title=”Post Contact Form”]


Mapping and GeolocationMany agritech apps rely on mapping and geolocation features to provide users with real-time information on crop conditions and soil moisture levels. It is important to design a mapping interface that is easy to use and provides accurate and up-to-date information. By prioritizing mapping and geolocation features in your app, you can provide users with valuable insights into the state of their crops and farms.


![PitangoUX UX/UI Design Agritask]


Triolla UX/UI Design Agritask


Alerts and NotificationsAgricultural operations often require timely and urgent responses to changing conditions, such as sudden changes in weather patterns or pest infestations. It is important to design an alert and notification system that can effectively communicate these changes to users. This includes designing clear and concise messages that provide actionable information and prompt users to take appropriate action.


![PitangoUX UX/UI Design Agritask]


Triolla UX/UI Design Agritask


Mobile OptimizationMany agricultural operations take place in remote or rural areas, where access to high-speed internet or desktop computers may be limited. It is important to design an app that is optimized for mobile devices, with a user interface that is easy to use on small screens and low-bandwidth connections. By prioritizing mobile optimization in your app, you can ensure that your users can access important information and take appropriate action from anywhere.


Integration with Other Agricultural SystemsAgricultural operations often rely on a range of other systems and technologies, such as weather sensors, soil moisture sensors, and irrigation systems. It is important to design an app that can effectively integrate with these other systems, providing users with a unified and streamlined experience. By prioritizing integration with other agricultural systems in your app, you can create a seamless and effective user experience.


In conclusion, designing a successful agritech app requires a deep understanding of user needs, data visualization, mapping and geolocation, alerts and notifications, mobile optimization, and integration with other agricultural systems. By prioritizing these key considerations in your design, you can create an app that is intuitive, effective, and easy to use. At Triolla, we have extensive experience in designing user-centered agritech experiences and can help you create an app that stands out in the competitive agritech market. Contact us today to learn more about our services and capabilities.

Unleash the Power of Your MVP to Accelerate Your Growth – UX Design for Startups


Uncover the Key Principles and Strategies for Designing an MVP That Captivates Your Target Audience and Boosts Your Startup’s Performance.


As a UX agency specializing in startup UX, we understand the importance of designing a successful MVP or prototype app or product. A well-designed MVP or prototype can make or break a startup’s success, and UX plays a critical role in that success. In this article, we will highlight the key bullet points to notice when designing a startup’s MVP or prototype.


Identify and Understand Your Target UsersOne of the essential factors in UX design is understanding your target users. Before starting to design your MVP or prototype, you need to identify your target audience and get to know their needs, expectations, and pain points. This information will help you design a product that meets the needs of your users, resulting in higher engagement and adoption rates.


Keep the MVP SimpleOne common mistake that startups make when designing their MVP is trying to cram too many features into it. Remember, the goal of the MVP is to validate your idea with minimal resources, time, and effort. Focus on developing the core features that solve the user’s pain points, and leave the nice-to-have features for later.


Focus on the User ExperienceThe user experience should be at the forefront of your design process. An excellent user experience means that your product is easy to use, intuitive, and enjoyable for your target audience. To achieve this, you need to design with the user in mind, which means taking into account their habits, preferences, and behaviors.


Design for Mobile FirstIn today’s digital age, mobile devices are the primary way people access the internet. As such, your MVP or prototype should be designed for mobile-first, with responsive design principles. This ensures that your product is accessible to a broader audience and delivers a seamless user experience across all devices.


[contact-form-7 id=”958e338″ title=”Post Contact Form”]


Test Early and OftenTesting is a critical step in the design process. Early testing allows you to validate your design assumptions and make changes before investing too much time and resources. Testing also helps you identify user pain points and opportunities for improvement. Regularly testing your MVP or prototype ensures that you’re creating a product that meets your user’s needs and expectations.


Implement AnalyticsAnalytics help you track user behavior, usage patterns, and other critical metrics. Implementing analytics from the start allows you to identify any issues or bottlenecks in your product’s flow and make necessary adjustments. Analytics also provide insights into what users like and don’t like about your product, which can help you refine your design and improve the user experience.


Be Consistent in Your DesignConsistency is key when designing a product. Ensure that all elements of your MVP or prototype are consistent, from the colors and typography to the layout and navigation. Consistency helps build trust and familiarity with your product, resulting in a better user experience.


Keep Your MVP or Prototype AgileAs a startup, your product is likely to evolve rapidly as you receive feedback and learn from your users. As such, it’s essential to keep your MVP or prototype agile, with the ability to adapt and iterate as necessary. This means designing a flexible product that can be easily modified and updated as you receive feedback.


ConclusionDesigning an MVP or prototype is a crucial step in the startup journey. A well-designed MVP or prototype can help validate your idea, attract investors, and acquire users. By keeping the user experience at the forefront of your design process, designing for mobile-first, testing regularly, implementing analytics, and keeping your product agile, you can ensure that your MVP or prototype is successful. At Triolla, we specialize in startup UX and can help you design a successful MVP or prototype. Contact us to learn more about our services.

The Essential Guide to Designing a Top – Performing Cyber App Mastering Cyber UX


Unleash the Full Potential of Your Cyber App with Key Insights and Strategies for User Experience, Security, and Accessibility.


As a UX agency specializing in cyber UX, we understand the critical role that UX plays in designing successful cyber apps and products. Cybersecurity is more critical than ever, and user experience can make or break a product’s security. In this article, we will highlight the key bullet points to notice when designing a cyber app or product.


Understand Your Users’ NeedsAs with any product or app, understanding your users’ needs is critical in designing a cyber app or product. In this case, it is especially important to consider the user’s level of technical expertise, knowledge of cybersecurity, and their security needs. Conduct user research to identify user needs, pain points, and behaviors to ensure that your design meets their expectations.


![ux for DeppKeep]


Prioritize SecuritySecurity is paramount in designing a cyber app or product. Consider the user’s data privacy and confidentiality, and ensure that your app or product meets the highest standards of cybersecurity. Work closely with security experts to ensure that your design incorporates the latest security protocols and best practices.


[contact-form-7 id=”958e338″ title=”Post Contact Form”]


Provide Clear and Concise InformationEffective communication is critical in cybersecurity. When designing your app or product, make sure that you provide clear and concise information about security risks, procedures, and best practices. Use simple language and visual aids to communicate complex concepts to users of all levels of technical expertise.


![ux for Armis]


Design for Ease of UseDesigning for ease of use is essential in cybersecurity. Users are more likely to follow security protocols when they are easy to use and understand. Design your app or product with an intuitive user interface, clear navigation, and simple workflows to help users complete security tasks with ease.


Use Feedback and AnalyticsUsing feedback and analytics is crucial in designing a cyber app or product. Analytics can help you understand how users interact with your product and identify areas for improvement. User feedback can also provide insights into user needs, pain points, and behaviors. Use both to continuously improve your design and meet user needs.


![ux for DeppKeep]


Design for AccessibilityDesigning for accessibility is critical in cybersecurity. Ensure that your app or product is accessible to users with disabilities, such as visual or hearing impairments. Consider the user’s needs when designing your app or product and provide alternative options for users who may not be able to use certain features.


Stay Up-to-Date with the Latest Cybersecurity TrendsStaying up-to-date with the latest cybersecurity trends is crucial in designing a cyber app or product. Cybersecurity is constantly evolving, and new threats and vulnerabilities are discovered every day. Stay current with the latest trends and best practices to ensure that your design incorporates the most effective cybersecurity measures.

Why Every Modern Company Needs a Stellar Dashboard UI – Insights from Triolla


We interact with them consistently. From morning check-ins to end-of-day reports, dashboards have become the unsung heroes in our professional lives, especially as the world leans into a hybrid working model post-pandemic. At Triolla, as leading UX designers serving Israeli startups and corporates, we believe in the potential of an expertly-crafted dashboard UI. Let’s delve into the art and science of creating an impeccable dashboard UI and understand how top brands nail it.


The Intriguing Origins of Dashboard UI


Ever pondered over the origins of the term ‘dashboard’? It harks back to the world of aviation and space. Pilots and astronauts rely on a control system, a ‘dashboard’ if you will, to navigate. But in a twist of nomenclature, it was the automotive sector that popularized the term. Traditionally, a dashboard referred to the panel indicating vital stats like speed, fuel, and temperature.


With the digital age in full swing by the early 2000s, the concept of a “Dashboard UI” emerged. In the world of UX UI portfolios, it represents a digital interface showcasing real-time Key Performance Indicators (KPIs). This is where decision-makers can gauge the pulse of their organization, thanks to this visually compelling data representation.


Mobile devices, novel design choices, and advanced data visualization like heat maps have since ushered in an era where dashboard UIs are more sophisticated and user-friendly.


Dashboard UI: More Than Just a Pretty Interface


Goal-Oriented Design is King


Despite evolving designs and trends, the core objective of dashboard UI design remains unaltered:


- Offer users a concise and clear snapshot of vital business metrics.

- Empower users with the data they need to make informed decisions efficiently.


By adhering to design conventions and best practices, designers at our UX studio and worldwide can craft dashboards that merge functionality with creativity. Think of it as an empowering tool steering your business towards its objectives.


[contact-form-7 id=”958e338″ title=”Post Contact Form”]


The Ubiquity of Modern Dashboard Designs


You might’ve noticed a striking similarity among modern dashboards, as if they’ve all been molded from the same UX UI portfolio blueprint. Why is that?


- Adherence to Standardization and Best PracticesOver the years, certain non-negotiable standards have been established for dashboard UIs. From lucid navigation and labeling to relevant data visualizations, designers leaning into these guidelines can inadvertently result in similar-looking UIs.

- Meeting User ExpectationsWith users now expecting specific features from their dashboards—like data drill-downs, custom views, and data filtering—designers work to integrate these elements. This user-centric design approach can sometimes result in UIs bearing a family resemblance.

- The Challenge of Design ConstraintsPresenting vast data amounts in a confined space is no easy feat. This often compels designers to embrace a minimalist design to aptly accommodate the data, which can again lead to similar UI aesthetics.

- Usability Trumps AllAt the heart of an effective dashboard UI is its ability to make data comprehension a breeze. Hence, designers often prioritize user-friendly features over aesthetic elements, leading to certain UI similarities.


However, it’s the nuanced touches that can set your dashboard UI apart. While the foundational structure might be standard, the play of branding elements, innovative typography, and colors can infuse uniqueness into your dashboard.


At Triolla, our expert UX designers prioritize crafting bespoke dashboard UIs that don’t just fit the mold but break it. After all, in a sea of similarities, it’s the unique touches that make a world of difference.
